562 static int is_file_in_memory(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path,
563  struct file *filep) {
564  size_t size = 0;
565  if ((filep->membuf = conn->ctx->callbacks.open_file == NULL ? NULL :
566  conn->ctx->callbacks.open_file(conn, path, &size)) != NULL) {
567  // NOTE: override filep->size only on success. Otherwise, it might break
568  // constructs like if (!mg_stat() || !mg_fopen()) ...
569  filep->size = size;
570  }
571  return filep->membuf != NULL;
572 }
573 
574 static int is_file_opened(const struct file *filep) {
575  return filep->membuf != NULL || filep->fp != NULL;
576 }
577 
578 static int mg_fopen(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path,
579  const char *mode, struct file *filep) {
580  if (!is_file_in_memory(conn, path, filep)) {
581 #ifdef _WIN32
582  wchar_t wbuf[PATH_MAX], wmode[20];
583  to_unicode(path, wbuf, ARRAY_SIZE(wbuf));
584  MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, mode, -1, wmode, ARRAY_SIZE(wmode));
585  filep->fp = _wfopen(wbuf, wmode);
586 #else
587  filep->fp = fopen(path, mode);
588 #endif
589  }
590 
591  return is_file_opened(filep);
592 }
593 
594 static void mg_fclose(struct file *filep) {
595  if (filep != NULL && filep->fp != NULL) {
596  fclose(filep->fp);
597  }
598 }

640 // Print error message to the opened error log stream.
641 static void cry(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *fmt, ...) {
642  char buf[MG_BUF_LEN], src_addr[IP_ADDR_STR_LEN];
643  va_list ap;
644  FILE *fp;
645  time_t timestamp;
646 
647  va_start(ap, fmt);
648  (void) vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), fmt, ap);
649  va_end(ap);
650 
651  // Do not lock when getting the callback value, here and below.
652  // I suppose this is fine, since function cannot disappear in the
653  // same way string option can.
654  if (conn->ctx->callbacks.log_message == NULL ||
655  conn->ctx->callbacks.log_message(conn, buf) == 0) {
656  fp = conn->ctx == NULL || conn->ctx->config[ERROR_LOG_FILE] == NULL ? NULL :
657  fopen(conn->ctx->config[ERROR_LOG_FILE], "a+");
658 
659  if (fp != NULL) {
660  flockfile(fp);
661  timestamp = time(NULL);
662 
663  sockaddr_to_string(src_addr, sizeof(src_addr), &conn->client.rsa);
664  fprintf(fp, "[%010lu] [error] [client %s] ", (unsigned long) timestamp,
665  src_addr);
666 
667  if (conn->request_info.request_method != NULL) {
668  fprintf(fp, "%s %s: ", conn->request_info.request_method,
669  conn->request_info.uri);
670  }
671 
672  fprintf(fp, "%s", buf);
673  fputc('\n', fp);
674  funlockfile(fp);
675  fclose(fp);
676  }
677  }
678 }

754 // Like snprintf(), but never returns negative value, or a value
755 // that is larger than a supplied buffer.
756 // Thanks to Adam Zeldis to pointing snprintf()-caused vulnerability
757 // in his audit report.
758 static int mg_vsnprintf(struct mg_connection *conn, char *buf, size_t buflen,
759  const char *fmt, va_list ap) {
760  int n;
761 
762  if (buflen == 0)
763  return 0;
764 
765  n = vsnprintf(buf, buflen, fmt, ap);
766 
767  if (n < 0) {
768  cry(conn, "vsnprintf error");
769  n = 0;
770  } else if (n >= (int) buflen) {
771  cry(conn, "truncating vsnprintf buffer: [%.*s]",
772  n > 200 ? 200 : n, buf);
773  n = (int) buflen - 1;
774  }
775  buf[n] = '\0';
776 
777  return n;
778 }

796 // Skip the characters until one of the delimiters characters found.
797 // 0-terminate resulting word. Skip the delimiter and following whitespaces.
798 // Advance pointer to buffer to the next word. Return found 0-terminated word.
799 // Delimiters can be quoted with quotechar.
800 static char *skip_quoted(char **buf, const char *delimiters,
801  const char *whitespace, char quotechar) {
802  char *p, *begin_word, *end_word, *end_whitespace;
803 
804  begin_word = *buf;
805  end_word = begin_word + strcspn(begin_word, delimiters);
806 
807  // Check for quotechar
808  if (end_word > begin_word) {
809  p = end_word - 1;
810  while (*p == quotechar) {
811  // If there is anything beyond end_word, copy it
812  if (*end_word == '\0') {
813 
814  *p = '\0';
815  break;
816  } else {
817  size_t end_off = strcspn(end_word + 1, delimiters);
818  memmove (p, end_word, end_off + 1);
819  p += end_off; // p must correspond to end_word - 1
820  end_word += end_off + 1;
821  }
822  }
823  for (p++; p < end_word; p++) {
824  *p = '\0';
825  }
826  }
827 
828  if (*end_word == '\0') {
829  *buf = end_word;
830  } else {
831  end_whitespace = end_word + 1 + strspn(end_word + 1, whitespace);
832 
833  for (p = end_word; p < end_whitespace; p++) {
834  *p = '\0';
835  }
836 
837  *buf = end_whitespace;
838  }
839 
840  return begin_word;
841 }
842 
843 // Simplified version of skip_quoted without quote char
844 // and whitespace == delimiters
845 static char *skip(char **buf, const char *delimiters) {
846  return skip_quoted(buf, delimiters, delimiters, 0);
847 }

866 // A helper function for traversing a comma separated list of values.
867 // It returns a list pointer shifted to the next value, or NULL if the end
868 // of the list found.
869 // Value is stored in val vector. If value has form "x=y", then eq_val
870 // vector is initialized to point to the "y" part, and val vector length
871 // is adjusted to point only to "x".
872 static const char *next_option(const char *list, struct vec *val,
873  struct vec *eq_val) {
874  if (list == NULL || *list == '\0') {
875  // End of the list
876  list = NULL;
877  } else {
878  val->ptr = list;
879  if ((list = strchr(val->ptr, ',')) != NULL) {
880  // Comma found. Store length and shift the list ptr
881  val->len = list - val->ptr;
882  list++;
883  } else {
884  // This value is the last one
885  list = val->ptr + strlen(val->ptr);
886  val->len = list - val->ptr;
887  }
888 
889  if (eq_val != NULL) {
890  // Value has form "x=y", adjust pointers and lengths
891  // so that val points to "x", and eq_val points to "y".
892  eq_val->len = 0;
893  eq_val->ptr = (const char *) memchr(val->ptr, '=', val->len);
894  if (eq_val->ptr != NULL) {
895  eq_val->ptr++; // Skip over '=' character
896  eq_val->len = val->ptr + val->len - eq_val->ptr;
897  val->len = (eq_val->ptr - val->ptr) - 1;
898  }
899  }
900  }
901 
902  return list;
903 }

905 // Perform case-insensitive match of string against pattern
906 static int match_prefix(const char *pattern, int pattern_len, const char *str) {
907  const char *or_str;
908  int i, j, len, res;
909 
910  if ((or_str = (const char *) memchr(pattern, '|', pattern_len)) != NULL) {
911  res = match_prefix(pattern, or_str - pattern, str);
912  return res > 0 ? res :
913  match_prefix(or_str + 1, (pattern + pattern_len) - (or_str + 1), str);
914  }
915 
916  i = j = 0;
917  res = -1;
918  for (; i < pattern_len; i++, j++) {
919  if (pattern[i] == '?' && str[j] != '\0') {
920  continue;
921  } else if (pattern[i] == '$') {
922  return str[j] == '\0' ? j : -1;
923  } else if (pattern[i] == '*') {
924  i++;
925  if (pattern[i] == '*') {
926  i++;
927  len = (int) strlen(str + j);
928  } else {
929  len = (int) strcspn(str + j, "/");
930  }
931  if (i == pattern_len) {
932  return j + len;
933  }
934  do {
935  res = match_prefix(pattern + i, pattern_len - i, str + j + len);
936  } while (res == -1 && len-- > 0);
937  return res == -1 ? -1 : j + res + len;
938  } else if (lowercase(&pattern[i]) != lowercase(&str[j])) {
939  return -1;
940  }
941  }
942  return j;
943 }
944 
945 // HTTP 1.1 assumes keep alive if "Connection:" header is not set
946 // This function must tolerate situations when connection info is not
947 // set up, for example if request parsing failed.
948 static int should_keep_alive(const struct mg_connection *conn) {
949  const char *http_version = conn->request_info.http_version;
950  const char *header = mg_get_header(conn, "Connection");
951  if (conn->must_close ||
952  conn->status_code == 401 ||
953  mg_strcasecmp(conn->ctx->config[ENABLE_KEEP_ALIVE], "yes") != 0 ||
954  (header != NULL && mg_strcasecmp(header, "keep-alive") != 0) ||
955  (header == NULL && http_version && strcmp(http_version, "1.1"))) {
956  return 0;
957  }
958  return 1;
959 }
960 
961 static const char *suggest_connection_header(const struct mg_connection *conn) {
962  return should_keep_alive(conn) ? "keep-alive" : "close";
963 }

970 static void send_http_error(struct mg_connection *conn, int status,
971  const char *reason, const char *fmt, ...) {
972  char buf[MG_BUF_LEN];
973  va_list ap;
974  int len = 0;
975 
976  conn->status_code = status;
977  if (conn->ctx->callbacks.http_error == NULL ||
978  conn->ctx->callbacks.http_error(conn, status)) {
979  buf[0] = '\0';
980 
981  // Errors 1xx, 204 and 304 MUST NOT send a body
982  if (status > 199 && status != 204 && status != 304) {
983  len = mg_snprintf(conn, buf, sizeof(buf), "Error %d: %s", status, reason);
984  buf[len++] = '\n';
985 
986  va_start(ap, fmt);
987  len += mg_vsnprintf(conn, buf + len, sizeof(buf) - len, fmt, ap);
988  va_end(ap);
989  }
990  DEBUG_TRACE(("[%s]", buf));
991 
992  mg_printf(conn, "HTTP/1.1 %d %s\r\n"
993  "Content-Length: %d\r\n"
994  "Connection: %s\r\n\r\n", status, reason, len,
995  suggest_connection_header(conn));
996  conn->num_bytes_sent += mg_printf(conn, "%s", buf);
997  }
998 }

1047 // For Windows, change all slashes to backslashes in path names.
1048 static void change_slashes_to_backslashes(char *path) {
1049  int i;
1050 
1051  for (i = 0; path[i] != '\0'; i++) {
1052  if (path[i] == '/')
1053  path[i] = '\\';
1054  // i > 0 check is to preserve UNC paths, like \\server\file.txt
1055  if (path[i] == '\\' && i > 0)
1056  while (path[i + 1] == '\\' || path[i + 1] == '/')
1057  (void) memmove(path + i + 1,
1058  path + i + 2, strlen(path + i + 1));
1059  }
1060 }

1062 // Encode 'path' which is assumed UTF-8 string, into UNICODE string.
1063 // wbuf and wbuf_len is a target buffer and its length.
1064 static void to_unicode(const char *path, wchar_t *wbuf, size_t wbuf_len) {
1065  char buf[PATH_MAX], buf2[PATH_MAX];
1066 
1067  mg_strlcpy(buf, path, sizeof(buf));
1068  change_slashes_to_backslashes(buf);
1069 
1070  // Convert to Unicode and back. If doubly-converted string does not
1071  // match the original, something is fishy, reject.
1072  memset(wbuf, 0, wbuf_len * sizeof(wchar_t));
1073  MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, buf, -1, wbuf, (int) wbuf_len);
1074  WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, wbuf, (int) wbuf_len, buf2, sizeof(buf2),
1075  NULL, NULL);
1076  if (strcmp(buf, buf2) != 0) {
1077  wbuf[0] = L'\0';
1078  }
1079 }

1137 // Windows happily opens files with some garbage at the end of file name.
1138 // For example, fopen("a.cgi ", "r") on Windows successfully opens
1139 // "a.cgi", despite one would expect an error back.
1140 // This function returns non-0 if path ends with some garbage.
1141 static int path_cannot_disclose_cgi(const char *path) {
1142  static const char *allowed_last_characters = "_-";

1147 static int mg_stat(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path,
1148  struct file *filep) {
1149  wchar_t wbuf[PATH_MAX];
1150  WIN32_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DATA info;
1151 
1152  if (!is_file_in_memory(conn, path, filep)) {
1153  to_unicode(path, wbuf, ARRAY_SIZE(wbuf));
1154  if (GetFileAttributesExW(wbuf, GetFileExInfoStandard, &info) != 0) {
1155  filep->size = MAKEUQUAD(info.nFileSizeLow, info.nFileSizeHigh);
1156  filep->modification_time = SYS2UNIX_TIME(
1157  info.ftLastWriteTime.dwLowDateTime,
1158  info.ftLastWriteTime.dwHighDateTime);
1159  filep->is_directory = info.dwFileAttributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY;
1160  // If file name is fishy, reset the file structure and return error.
1161  // Note it is important to reset, not just return the error, cause
1162  // functions like is_file_opened() check the struct.
1163  if (!filep->is_directory && !path_cannot_disclose_cgi(path)) {
1164  memset(filep, 0, sizeof(*filep));
1165  }
1166  }
1167  }
1168 
1169  return filep->membuf != NULL || filep->modification_time != 0;
1170 }

1191 // Implementation of POSIX opendir/closedir/readdir for Windows.
1192 static DIR * opendir(const char *name) {
1193  DIR *dir = NULL;
1194  wchar_t wpath[PATH_MAX];
1195  DWORD attrs;
1196 
1197  if (name == NULL) {
1198  SetLastError(ERROR_BAD_ARGUMENTS);
1199  } else if ((dir = (DIR *) malloc(sizeof(*dir))) == NULL) {
1200  SetLastError(ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY);
1201  } else {
1202  to_unicode(name, wpath, ARRAY_SIZE(wpath));
1203  attrs = GetFileAttributesW(wpath);
1204  if (attrs != 0xFFFFFFFF &&
1205  ((attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY) == FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY)) {

1289 static pid_t spawn_process(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *prog,
1290  char *envblk, char *envp[], int fdin,
1291  int fdout, const char *dir) {
1292  HANDLE me;
1293  char *p, *interp, full_interp[PATH_MAX], full_dir[PATH_MAX],
1294  cmdline[PATH_MAX], buf[PATH_MAX];
1295  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
1296  STARTUPINFOA si;
1297  PROCESS_INFORMATION pi = { 0 };
1298 
1299  (void) envp;
1300 
1301  memset(&si, 0, sizeof(si));
1302  si.cb = sizeof(si);
1303 
1304  // TODO(lsm): redirect CGI errors to the error log file
1305  si.dwFlags = STARTF_USESTDHANDLES | STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW;
1306  si.wShowWindow = SW_HIDE;
1307 
1308  me = GetCurrentProcess();
1309  DuplicateHandle(me, (HANDLE) _get_osfhandle(fdin), me,
1310  &si.hStdInput, 0, TRUE, DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS);
1311  DuplicateHandle(me, (HANDLE) _get_osfhandle(fdout), me,
1312  &si.hStdOutput, 0, TRUE, DUPLICATE_SAME_ACCESS);

1315  interp = conn->ctx->config[CGI_INTERPRETER];

1317  buf[0] = buf[1] = '\0';
1318 
1319  // Read the first line of the script into the buffer
1320  snprintf(cmdline, sizeof(cmdline), "%s%c%s", dir, '/', prog);
1321  if (mg_fopen(conn, cmdline, "r", &file)) {
1322  p = (char *) file.membuf;
1323  mg_fgets(buf, sizeof(buf), &file, &p);
1324  mg_fclose(&file);
1325  buf[sizeof(buf) - 1] = '\0';
1326  }
1327 
1328  if (buf[0] == '#' && buf[1] == '!') {
1329  trim_trailing_whitespaces(buf + 2);
1330  } else {
1331  buf[2] = '\0';
1332  }
1333  interp = buf + 2;
1334  }
1335 
1336  if (interp[0] != '\0') {

1338  interp = full_interp;

1340  GetFullPathNameA(dir, sizeof(full_dir), full_dir, NULL);
1341 
1342  mg_snprintf(conn, cmdline, sizeof(cmdline), "%s%s\"%s\\%s\"",
1343  interp, interp[0] == '\0' ? "" : " ", full_dir, prog);
1344 
1345  DEBUG_TRACE(("Running [%s]", cmdline));
1346  if (CreateProcessA(NULL, cmdline, NULL, NULL, TRUE,
1347  CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, envblk, NULL, &si, &pi) == 0) {
1348  cry(conn, "%s: CreateProcess(%s): %ld",

1352 
1353  (void) CloseHandle(si.hStdOutput);
1354  (void) CloseHandle(si.hStdInput);

1386 int mg_start_thread(mg_thread_func_t func, void *param) {
1387  pthread_t thread_id;
1388  pthread_attr_t attr;
1389  int result;
1390  struct mg_context* ctx = param;
1391  char* stacksize = ctx->config[THREAD_STACK_SIZE];
1392  char* priority = ctx->config[THREAD_PRIORITY];
1393  char* policy = ctx->config[THREAD_POLICY];
1394  int noinheritsched = 0;
1395 
1396  (void) pthread_attr_init(&attr);
1397  (void) pthread_attr_setdetachstate(&attr, PTHREAD_CREATE_DETACHED);
1398 
1399 #if USE_STACK_SIZE > 1
1400  // Compile-time option to control stack size, e.g. -DUSE_STACK_SIZE=16384; Can be overridden
1401  if (stacksize == NULL)
1402  (void) pthread_attr_setstacksize(&attr, USE_STACK_SIZE);
1403 #endif
1404 
1405  if (stacksize != NULL) {
1406  size_t size = atoi(stacksize);
1407  (void) pthread_attr_setstacksize(&attr, size);
1408  }
1409 
1410  if (priority != NULL) {
1411  struct sched_param sched_param;
1412  memset(&sched_param, 0, sizeof(sched_param));
1413  sched_param.sched_priority = atoi(priority);
1414  (void) pthread_attr_setschedparam(&attr, &sched_param);
1415  noinheritsched = 1;
1416  }
1417 
1418  if (policy != NULL) {
1419  int p_policy;
1420  (void) pthread_attr_getschedpolicy(&attr, &p_policy);
1421 
1422  switch (policy[0]) {
1423  case 'o':
1424  p_policy = SCHED_OTHER;
1425  break;
1426  case 'f':
1427  p_policy = SCHED_FIFO;
1428  break;
1429  case 'r':
1430  p_policy = SCHED_RR;
1431  break;
1432 #if defined(_POSIX_SPORADIC_SERVER) || defined(_POSIX_THREAD_SPORADIC_SERVER)
1433  case 's':
1434  p_policy = SCHED_SPORADIC;
1435  break;
1436 #endif
1437  default:
1438  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: Unknown scheduler: %s", __func__, policy);
1439  break;
1440  }
1441 
1442  (void) pthread_attr_setschedpolicy(&attr, p_policy);
1443 
1444  noinheritsched = 1;
1445  }
1446 
1447  if (noinheritsched != 0) {
1448  (void) pthread_attr_setinheritsched(&attr, PTHREAD_EXPLICIT_SCHED);
1449  }
1450 
1451  result = pthread_create(&thread_id, &attr, func, param);
1452  pthread_attr_destroy(&attr);
1453 
1454  return result;
1455 }

1457 #ifndef NO_CGI
1458 static pid_t spawn_process(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *prog,
1459  char *envblk, char *envp[], int fdin,
1460  int fdout, const char *dir) {
1461  pid_t pid;
1462  const char *interp;
1463 
1464  (void) envblk;
1465 
1466  if ((pid = fork()) == -1) {
1467  // Parent
1468  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error, "fork(): %s", strerror(ERRNO));
1469  } else if (pid == 0) {
1470  // Child
1471  if (chdir(dir) != 0) {
1472  cry(conn, "%s: chdir(%s): %s", __func__, dir, strerror(ERRNO));
1473  } else if (dup2(fdin, 0) == -1) {
1474  cry(conn, "%s: dup2(%d, 0): %s", __func__, fdin, strerror(ERRNO));
1475  } else if (dup2(fdout, 1) == -1) {
1476  cry(conn, "%s: dup2(%d, 1): %s", __func__, fdout, strerror(ERRNO));
1477  } else {
1478  // Not redirecting stderr to stdout, to avoid output being littered
1479  // with the error messages.
1480  (void) close(fdin);
1481  (void) close(fdout);
1482 
1483  // After exec, all signal handlers are restored to their default values,
1484  // with one exception of SIGCHLD. According to POSIX.1-2001 and Linux's
1485  // implementation, SIGCHLD's handler will leave unchanged after exec
1486  // if it was set to be ignored. Restore it to default action.
1487  signal(SIGCHLD, SIG_DFL);
1488 
1489  interp = conn->ctx->config[CGI_INTERPRETER];
1490  if (interp == NULL) {
1491  (void) execle(prog, prog, NULL, envp);
1492  cry(conn, "%s: execle(%s): %s", __func__, prog, strerror(ERRNO));
1493  } else {
1494  (void) execle(interp, interp, prog, NULL, envp);
1495  cry(conn, "%s: execle(%s %s): %s", __func__, interp, prog,
1496  strerror(ERRNO));
1497  }
1498  }
1499  exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
1500  }
1501 
1502  return pid;
1503 }
1504 #endif // !NO_CGI

1516 #ifndef HAVE_POLL
1517 static int poll(struct pollfd *pfd, int n, int milliseconds) {
1518  struct timeval tv;
1519  fd_set set;
1520  int i, result;
1521  SOCKET maxfd = 0;
1522 
1523  tv.tv_sec = milliseconds / 1000;
1524  tv.tv_usec = (milliseconds % 1000) * 1000;
1525  FD_ZERO(&set);
1526 
1527  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
1528  FD_SET((SOCKET) pfd[i].fd, &set);
1529  pfd[i].revents = 0;
1530 
1531  if (pfd[i].fd > maxfd) {
1532  maxfd = pfd[i].fd;
1533  }
1534  }
1535 
1536  if ((result = select(maxfd + 1, &set, NULL, NULL, &tv)) > 0) {
1537  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
1538  if (FD_ISSET(pfd[i].fd, &set)) {
1539  pfd[i].revents = POLLIN;
1540  }
1541  }
1542  }
1543 
1544  return result;
1545 }
1546 #endif // HAVE_POLL

1548 // Write data to the IO channel - opened file descriptor, socket or SSL
1549 // descriptor. Return number of bytes written.
1550 static int64_t push(FILE *fp, SOCKET sock, SSL *ssl, const char *buf,
1551  int64_t len) {
1552  int64_t sent;
1553  int n, k;
1554 
1555  (void) ssl; // Get rid of warning
1556  sent = 0;
1557  while (sent < len) {
1558 
1559  // How many bytes we send in this iteration
1560  k = len - sent > INT_MAX ? INT_MAX : (int) (len - sent);
1561 
1562 #ifndef NO_SSL
1563  if (ssl != NULL) {
1564  n = SSL_write(ssl, buf + sent, k);
1565  } else
1566 #endif
1567  if (fp != NULL) {
1568  n = (int) fwrite(buf + sent, 1, (size_t) k, fp);
1569  if (ferror(fp))
1570  n = -1;
1571  } else {
1572  n = send(sock, buf + sent, (size_t) k, MSG_NOSIGNAL);
1573  }
1574 
1575  if (n <= 0)
1576  break;
1577 
1578  sent += n;
1579  }
1580 
1581  return sent;
1582 }
1583 
1584 // Read from IO channel - opened file descriptor, socket, or SSL descriptor.
1585 // Return negative value on error, or number of bytes read on success.
1586 static int pull(FILE *fp, struct mg_connection *conn, char *buf, int len) {
1587  int nread;
1588 
1589  if (fp != NULL) {
1590  // Use read() instead of fread(), because if we're reading from the CGI
1591  // pipe, fread() may block until IO buffer is filled up. We cannot afford
1592  // to block and must pass all read bytes immediately to the client.
1593  nread = read(fileno(fp), buf, (size_t) len);
1594 #ifndef NO_SSL
1595  } else if (conn->ssl != NULL) {
1596  nread = SSL_read(conn->ssl, buf, len);
1597 #endif
1598  } else {
1599  nread = recv(conn->client.sock, buf, (size_t) len, 0);
1600  }
1601 
1602  return conn->ctx->stop_flag ? -1 : nread;
1603 }
1604 
1605 static int pull_all(FILE *fp, struct mg_connection *conn, char *buf, int len) {
1606  int n, nread = 0;
1607 
1608  while (len > 0 && conn->ctx->stop_flag == 0) {
1609  n = pull(fp, conn, buf + nread, len);
1610  if (n < 0) {
1611  nread = n; // Propagate the error
1612  break;
1613  } else if (n == 0) {
1614  break; // No more data to read
1615  } else {
1616  conn->consumed_content += n;
1617  nread += n;
1618  len -= n;
1619  }
1620  }
1621 
1622  return nread;
1623 }
1624 
1625 int mg_read(struct mg_connection *conn, void *buf, size_t len) {
1626  int n, buffered_len, nread;
1627  const char *body;
1628 
1629  // If Content-Length is not set, read until socket is closed
1630  if (conn->consumed_content == 0 && conn->content_len == 0) {
1631  conn->content_len = INT64_MAX;
1632  conn->must_close = 1;
1633  }
1634 
1635  nread = 0;
1636  if (conn->consumed_content < conn->content_len) {
1637  // Adjust number of bytes to read.
1638  int64_t to_read = conn->content_len - conn->consumed_content;
1639  if (to_read < (int64_t) len) {
1640  len = (size_t) to_read;
1641  }
1642 
1643  // Return buffered data
1644  body = conn->buf + conn->request_len + conn->consumed_content;
1645  buffered_len = &conn->buf[conn->data_len] - body;
1646  if (buffered_len > 0) {
1647  if (len < (size_t) buffered_len) {
1648  buffered_len = (int) len;
1649  }
1650  memcpy(buf, body, (size_t) buffered_len);
1651  len -= buffered_len;
1652  conn->consumed_content += buffered_len;
1653  nread += buffered_len;
1654  buf = (char *) buf + buffered_len;
1655  }
1656 
1657  // We have returned all buffered data. Read new data from the remote socket.
1658  n = pull_all(NULL, conn, (char *) buf, (int) len);
1659  nread = n >= 0 ? nread + n : n;
1660  }
1661  return nread;
1662 }
1663 
1664 int mg_write(struct mg_connection *conn, const void *buf, size_t len) {
1665  time_t now;
1666  int64_t n, total, allowed;
1667 
1668  if (conn->throttle > 0) {
1669  if ((now = time(NULL)) != conn->last_throttle_time) {
1670  conn->last_throttle_time = now;
1671  conn->last_throttle_bytes = 0;
1672  }
1673  allowed = conn->throttle - conn->last_throttle_bytes;
1674  if (allowed > (int64_t) len) {
1675  allowed = len;
1676  }
1677  if ((total = push(NULL, conn->client.sock, conn->ssl, (const char *) buf,
1678  (int64_t) allowed)) == allowed) {
1679  buf = (char *) buf + total;
1680  conn->last_throttle_bytes += total;
1681  while (total < (int64_t) len && conn->ctx->stop_flag == 0) {
1682  allowed = conn->throttle > (int64_t) len - total ?
1683  (int64_t) len - total : conn->throttle;
1684  if ((n = push(NULL, conn->client.sock, conn->ssl, (const char *) buf,
1685  (int64_t) allowed)) != allowed) {
1686  break;
1687  }
1688  sleep(1);
1689  conn->last_throttle_bytes = allowed;
1690  conn->last_throttle_time = time(NULL);
1691  buf = (char *) buf + n;
1692  total += n;
1693  }
1694  }
1695  } else {
1696  total = push(NULL, conn->client.sock, conn->ssl, (const char *) buf,
1697  (int64_t) len);
1698  }
1699  return (int) total;
1700 }

1702 // Alternative alloc_vprintf() for non-compliant C runtimes
1703 static int alloc_vprintf2(char **buf, const char *fmt, va_list ap) {
1704  va_list ap_copy;
1705  int size = MG_BUF_LEN;
1706  int len = -1;
1707 
1708  *buf = NULL;
1709  while (len == -1) {
1710  if (*buf) free(*buf);
1711  *buf = malloc(size *= 4);
1712  if (!*buf) break;
1713  va_copy(ap_copy, ap);
1714  len = vsnprintf(*buf, size, fmt, ap_copy);
1715  }
1716 
1717  return len;
1718 }
1719 
1720 // Print message to buffer. If buffer is large enough to hold the message,
1721 // return buffer. If buffer is to small, allocate large enough buffer on heap,
1722 // and return allocated buffer.
1723 static int alloc_vprintf(char **buf, size_t size, const char *fmt, va_list ap) {
1724  va_list ap_copy;
1725  int len;
1726 
1727  // Windows is not standard-compliant, and vsnprintf() returns -1 if
1728  // buffer is too small. Also, older versions of msvcrt.dll do not have
1729  // _vscprintf(). However, if size is 0, vsnprintf() behaves correctly.
1730  // Therefore, we make two passes: on first pass, get required message length.
1731  // On second pass, actually print the message.
1732  va_copy(ap_copy, ap);
1733  len = vsnprintf(NULL, 0, fmt, ap_copy);
1734 
1735  if (len < 0) {
1736  // C runtime is not standard compliant, vsnprintf() returned -1.
1737  // Switch to alternative code path that uses incremental allocations.
1738  va_copy(ap_copy, ap);
1739  len = alloc_vprintf2(buf, fmt, ap);
1740  } else if (len > (int) size &&
1741  (size = len + 1) > 0 &&
1742  (*buf = (char *) malloc(size)) == NULL) {
1743  len = -1; // Allocation failed, mark failure
1744  } else {
1745  va_copy(ap_copy, ap);
1746  vsnprintf(*buf, size, fmt, ap_copy);
1747  }
1748 
1749  return len;
1750 }
1751 
1752 static int mg_vprintf(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *fmt, va_list ap) {
1753  char mem[MG_BUF_LEN], *buf = mem;
1754  int len;
1755 
1756  if ((len = alloc_vprintf(&buf, sizeof(mem), fmt, ap)) > 0) {
1757  len = mg_write(conn, buf, (size_t) len);
1758  }
1759  if (buf != mem && buf != NULL) {
1760  free(buf);
1761  }
1762 
1763  return len;
1764 }
1765 
1766 int mg_printf(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *fmt, ...) {
1767  va_list ap;
1768  va_start(ap, fmt);
1769  return mg_vprintf(conn, fmt, ap);
1770 }

1772 int mg_url_decode(const char *src, int src_len, char *dst,
1773  int dst_len, int is_form_url_encoded) {
1774  int i, j, a, b;
1775 #define HEXTOI(x) (isdigit(x) ? x - '0' : x - 'W')
1776 
1777  for (i = j = 0; i < src_len && j < dst_len - 1; i++, j++) {
1778  if (src[i] == '%' && i < src_len - 2 &&
1779  isxdigit(* (const unsigned char *) (src + i + 1)) &&
1780  isxdigit(* (const unsigned char *) (src + i + 2))) {
1781  a = tolower(* (const unsigned char *) (src + i + 1));
1782  b = tolower(* (const unsigned char *) (src + i + 2));
1783  dst[j] = (char) ((HEXTOI(a) << 4) | HEXTOI(b));
1784  i += 2;
1785  } else if (is_form_url_encoded && src[i] == '+') {
1786  dst[j] = ' ';
1787  } else {
1788  dst[j] = src[i];
1789  }
1790  }
1791 
1792  dst[j] = '\0'; // Null-terminate the destination
1793 
1794  return i >= src_len ? j : -1;
1795 }

1797 int mg_get_var(const char *data, size_t data_len, const char *name,
1798  char *dst, size_t dst_len) {
1799  const char *p, *e, *s;
1800  size_t name_len;
1801  int len;
1802 
1803  if (dst == NULL || dst_len == 0) {
1804  len = -2;
1805  } else if (data == NULL || name == NULL || data_len == 0) {
1806  len = -1;
1807  dst[0] = '\0';
1808  } else {
1809  name_len = strlen(name);
1810  e = data + data_len;
1811  len = -1;
1812  dst[0] = '\0';
1813 
1814  // data is "var1=val1&var2=val2...". Find variable first
1815  for (p = data; p + name_len < e; p++) {
1816  if ((p == data || p[-1] == '&') && p[name_len] == '=' &&
1817  !mg_strncasecmp(name, p, name_len)) {
1818 
1819  // Point p to variable value
1820  p += name_len + 1;
1821 
1822  // Point s to the end of the value
1823  s = (const char *) memchr(p, '&', (size_t)(e - p));
1824  if (s == NULL) {
1825  s = e;
1826  }
1827  assert(s >= p);
1828 
1829  // Decode variable into destination buffer
1830  len = mg_url_decode(p, (size_t)(s - p), dst, dst_len, 1);
1831 
1832  // Redirect error code from -1 to -2 (destination buffer too small).
1833  if (len == -1) {
1834  len = -2;
1835  }
1836  break;
1837  }
1838  }
1839  }
1840 
1841  return len;

1844 int mg_get_cookie(const char *cookie_header, const char *var_name,
1845  char *dst, size_t dst_size) {
1846  const char *s, *p, *end;
1847  int name_len, len = -1;
1848 
1849  if (dst == NULL || dst_size == 0) {
1850  len = -2;
1851  } else if (var_name == NULL || (s = cookie_header) == NULL) {
1852  len = -1;
1853  dst[0] = '\0';
1854  } else {
1855  name_len = (int) strlen(var_name);
1856  end = s + strlen(s);
1857  dst[0] = '\0';
1858 
1859  for (; (s = mg_strcasestr(s, var_name)) != NULL; s += name_len) {
1860  if (s[name_len] == '=') {
1861  s += name_len + 1;
1862  if ((p = strchr(s, ' ')) == NULL)
1863  p = end;
1864  if (p[-1] == ';')
1865  p--;
1866  if (*s == '"' && p[-1] == '"' && p > s + 1) {
1867  s++;
1868  p--;
1869  }
1870  if ((size_t) (p - s) < dst_size) {
1871  len = p - s;
1872  mg_strlcpy(dst, s, (size_t) len + 1);
1873  } else {
1874  len = -3;
1875  }
1876  break;
1877  }
1878  }
1879  }
1880  return len;
1881 }

1883 static void convert_uri_to_file_name(struct mg_connection *conn, char *buf,
1884  size_t buf_len, struct file *filep) {
1885  struct vec a, b;
1886  const char *rewrite, *uri = conn->request_info.uri,
1887  *root = conn->ctx->config[DOCUMENT_ROOT];
1888  char *p;
1889  int match_len;
1890  char gz_path[PATH_MAX];
1891  char const* accept_encoding;
1892 
1893  // Using buf_len - 1 because memmove() for PATH_INFO may shift part
1894  // of the path one byte on the right.
1895  // If document_root is NULL, leave the file empty.
1896  mg_snprintf(conn, buf, buf_len - 1, "%s%s",
1897  root == NULL ? "" : root,
1898  root == NULL ? "" : uri);
1899 
1900  rewrite = conn->ctx->config[REWRITE];
1901  while ((rewrite = next_option(rewrite, &a, &b)) != NULL) {
1902  if ((match_len = match_prefix(a.ptr, a.len, uri)) > 0) {
1903  mg_snprintf(conn, buf, buf_len - 1, "%.*s%s", (int) b.len, b.ptr,
1904  uri + match_len);
1905  break;
1906  }
1907  }
1908 
1909  if (mg_stat(conn, buf, filep)) return;
1910 
1911  // if we can't find the actual file, look for the file
1912  // with the same name but a .gz extension. If we find it,
1913  // use that and set the gzipped flag in the file struct
1914  // to indicate that the response need to have the content-
1915  // encoding: gzip header
1916  // we can only do this if the browser declares support
1917  if ((accept_encoding = mg_get_header(conn, "Accept-Encoding")) != NULL) {
1918  if (strstr(accept_encoding,"gzip") != NULL) {
1919  snprintf(gz_path, sizeof(gz_path), "%s.gz", buf);
1920  if (mg_stat(conn, gz_path, filep)) {
1921  filep->gzipped = 1;
1922  return;
1923  }
1924  }
1925  }
1926 
1927  // Support PATH_INFO for CGI scripts.
1928  for (p = buf + strlen(buf); p > buf + 1; p--) {
1929  if (*p == '/') {
1930  *p = '\0';
1931  if (match_prefix(conn->ctx->config[CGI_EXTENSIONS],
1932  strlen(conn->ctx->config[CGI_EXTENSIONS]), buf) > 0 &&
1933  mg_stat(conn, buf, filep)) {
1934  // Shift PATH_INFO block one character right, e.g.
1935  // "/x.cgi/foo/bar\x00" => "/x.cgi\x00/foo/bar\x00"
1936  // conn->path_info is pointing to the local variable "path" declared
1937  // in handle_request(), so PATH_INFO is not valid after
1938  // handle_request returns.
1939  conn->path_info = p + 1;
1940  memmove(p + 2, p + 1, strlen(p + 1) + 1); // +1 is for trailing \0
1941  p[1] = '/';
1942  break;
1943  } else {
1944  *p = '/';
1945  }
1946  }
1947  }
1948 }
1949 
1950 // Check whether full request is buffered. Return:
1951 // -1 if request is malformed
1952 // 0 if request is not yet fully buffered
1953 // >0 actual request length, including last \r\n\r\n
1954 static int get_request_len(const char *buf, int buflen) {
1955  const char *s, *e;
1956  int len = 0;
1957 
1958  for (s = buf, e = s + buflen - 1; len <= 0 && s < e; s++)
1959  // Control characters are not allowed but >=128 is.
1960  if (!isprint(* (const unsigned char *) s) && *s != '\r' &&
1961  *s != '\n' && * (const unsigned char *) s < 128) {
1962  len = -1;
1963  break; // [i_a] abort scan as soon as one malformed character is found;
1964  // don't let subsequent \r\n\r\n win us over anyhow
1965  } else if (s[0] == '\n' && s[1] == '\n') {
1966  len = (int) (s - buf) + 2;
1967  } else if (s[0] == '\n' && &s[1] < e &&
1968  s[1] == '\r' && s[2] == '\n') {
1969  len = (int) (s - buf) + 3;
1970  }
1971 
1972  return len;
1973 }

1980  if (!strcmp(s, month_names[i]))
1981  return (int) i;

1986 static int num_leap_years(int year) {
1987  return year / 4 - year / 100 + year / 400;
1988 }

1990 // Parse UTC date-time string, and return the corresponding time_t value.
1991 static time_t parse_date_string(const char *datetime) {
1992  static const unsigned short days_before_month[] = {
1993  0, 31, 59, 90, 120, 151, 181, 212, 243, 273, 304, 334
1994  };
1995  char month_str[32];
1996  int second, minute, hour, day, month, year, leap_days, days;
1997  time_t result = (time_t) 0;
1998 
1999  if (((sscanf(datetime, "%d/%3s/%d %d:%d:%d",
2000  &day, month_str, &year, &hour, &minute, &second) == 6) ||
2001  (sscanf(datetime, "%d %3s %d %d:%d:%d",
2002  &day, month_str, &year, &hour, &minute, &second) == 6) ||
2003  (sscanf(datetime, "%*3s, %d %3s %d %d:%d:%d",
2004  &day, month_str, &year, &hour, &minute, &second) == 6) ||
2005  (sscanf(datetime, "%d-%3s-%d %d:%d:%d",
2006  &day, month_str, &year, &hour, &minute, &second) == 6)) &&
2007  year > 1970 &&
2008  (month = get_month_index(month_str)) != -1) {
2009  leap_days = num_leap_years(year) - num_leap_years(1970);
2010  year -= 1970;
2011  days = year * 365 + days_before_month[month] + (day - 1) + leap_days;
2012  result = days * 24 * 3600 + hour * 3600 + minute * 60 + second;
2013  }
2014 
2015  return result;
2016 }

2018 // Protect against directory disclosure attack by removing '..',

2020 static void remove_double_dots_and_double_slashes(char *s) {
2021  char *p = s;

2023  while (*s != '\0') {
2024  *p++ = *s++;
2025  if (s[-1] == '/' || s[-1] == '\\') {
2026  // Skip all following slashes, backslashes and double-dots
2027  while (s[0] != '\0') {
2028  if (s[0] == '/' || s[0] == '\\') {
2029  s++;
2030  } else if (s[0] == '.' && s[1] == '.') {
2031  s += 2;
2032  } else {
2033  break;
2034  }
2035  }
2036  }
2037  }
2038  *p = '\0';
2039 }

2267 static void MD5Update(MD5_CTX *ctx, unsigned char const *buf, unsigned len) {
2268  uint32_t t;
2269 
2270  t = ctx->bits[0];
2271  if ((ctx->bits[0] = t + ((uint32_t) len << 3)) < t)
2272  ctx->bits[1]++;
2273  ctx->bits[1] += len >> 29;
2274 
2275  t = (t >> 3) & 0x3f;
2276 
2277  if (t) {
2278  unsigned char *p = (unsigned char *) ctx->in + t;
2279 
2280  t = 64 - t;
2281  if (len < t) {
2282  memcpy(p, buf, len);
2283  return;
2284  }
2285  memcpy(p, buf, t);
2286  byteReverse(ctx->in, 16);
2287  MD5Transform(ctx->buf, (uint32_t *) ctx->in);
2288  buf += t;
2289  len -= t;
2290  }
2291 
2292  while (len >= 64) {
2293  memcpy(ctx->in, buf, 64);
2294  byteReverse(ctx->in, 16);
2295  MD5Transform(ctx->buf, (uint32_t *) ctx->in);
2296  buf += 64;
2297  len -= 64;
2298  }
2299 
2300  memcpy(ctx->in, buf, len);
2301 }
2302 
2303 static void MD5Final(unsigned char digest[16], MD5_CTX *ctx) {
2304  unsigned count;
2305  unsigned char *p;
2306  uint32_t *a;
2307 
2308  count = (ctx->bits[0] >> 3) & 0x3F;
2309 
2310  p = ctx->in + count;
2311  *p++ = 0x80;
2312  count = 64 - 1 - count;
2313  if (count < 8) {
2314  memset(p, 0, count);
2315  byteReverse(ctx->in, 16);
2316  MD5Transform(ctx->buf, (uint32_t *) ctx->in);
2317  memset(ctx->in, 0, 56);
2318  } else {
2319  memset(p, 0, count - 8);
2320  }
2321  byteReverse(ctx->in, 14);
2322 
2323  a = (uint32_t *)ctx->in;
2324  a[14] = ctx->bits[0];
2325  a[15] = ctx->bits[1];
2326 
2327  MD5Transform(ctx->buf, (uint32_t *) ctx->in);
2328  byteReverse((unsigned char *) ctx->buf, 4);
2329  memcpy(digest, ctx->buf, 16);
2330  memset((char *) ctx, 0, sizeof(*ctx));
2331 }
2332 #endif // !HAVE_MD5
2333 
2334 // Stringify binary data. Output buffer must be twice as big as input,
2335 // because each byte takes 2 bytes in string representation
2336 static void bin2str(char *to, const unsigned char *p, size_t len) {
2337  static const char *hex = "0123456789abcdef";
2338 
2339  for (; len--; p++) {
2340  *to++ = hex[p[0] >> 4];
2341  *to++ = hex[p[0] & 0x0f];
2342  }
2343  *to = '\0';
2344 }
2345 
2346 // Return stringified MD5 hash for list of strings. Buffer must be 33 bytes.
2347 char *mg_md5(char buf[33], ...) {
2348  unsigned char hash[16];
2349  const char *p;
2350  va_list ap;
2351  MD5_CTX ctx;
2352 
2353  MD5Init(&ctx);
2354 
2355  va_start(ap, buf);
2356  while ((p = va_arg(ap, const char *)) != NULL) {
2357  MD5Update(&ctx, (const unsigned char *) p, (unsigned) strlen(p));
2358  }
2359  va_end(ap);
2360 
2361  MD5Final(hash, &ctx);
2362  bin2str(buf, hash, sizeof(hash));
2363  return buf;
2364 }

2366 // Check the user's password, return 1 if OK
2367 static int check_password(const char *method, const char *ha1, const char *uri,
2368  const char *nonce, const char *nc, const char *cnonce,
2369  const char *qop, const char *response) {
2370  char ha2[32 + 1], expected_response[32 + 1];
2371 
2372  // Some of the parameters may be NULL
2373  if (method == NULL || nonce == NULL || nc == NULL || cnonce == NULL ||
2374  qop == NULL || response == NULL) {
2375  return 0;
2376  }
2377 
2378  // NOTE(lsm): due to a bug in MSIE, we do not compare the URI
2379  // TODO(lsm): check for authentication timeout
2380  if (// strcmp(dig->uri, c->ouri) != 0 ||
2381  strlen(response) != 32
2382  // || now - strtoul(dig->nonce, NULL, 10) > 3600
2383  ) {
2384  return 0;
2385  }
2386 
2387  mg_md5(ha2, method, ":", uri, NULL);
2388  mg_md5(expected_response, ha1, ":", nonce, ":", nc,
2389  ":", cnonce, ":", qop, ":", ha2, NULL);
2390 
2391  return mg_strcasecmp(response, expected_response) == 0;
2392 }

2394 // Use the global passwords file, if specified by auth_gpass option,
2395 // or search for .htpasswd in the requested directory.
2396 static void open_auth_file(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path,
2397  struct file *filep) {
2398  char name[PATH_MAX];
2399  const char *p, *e, *gpass = conn->ctx->config[GLOBAL_PASSWORDS_FILE];
2400  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
2401 
2402  if (gpass != NULL) {
2403  // Use global passwords file
2404  if (!mg_fopen(conn, gpass, "r", filep)) {
2405  cry(conn, "fopen(%s): %s", gpass, strerror(ERRNO));
2406  }
2407  // Important: using local struct file to test path for is_directory flag.
2408  // If filep is used, mg_stat() makes it appear as if auth file was opened.
2409  } else if (mg_stat(conn, path, &file) && file.is_directory) {
2410  mg_snprintf(conn, name, sizeof(name), "%s%c%s",
2411  path, '/', PASSWORDS_FILE_NAME);
2412  mg_fopen(conn, name, "r", filep);
2413  } else {
2414  // Try to find .htpasswd in requested directory.
2415  for (p = path, e = p + strlen(p) - 1; e > p; e--)
2416  if (e[0] == '/')
2417  break;
2418  mg_snprintf(conn, name, sizeof(name), "%.*s%c%s",
2419  (int) (e - p), p, '/', PASSWORDS_FILE_NAME);
2420  mg_fopen(conn, name, "r", filep);
2421  }
2422 }

2424 // Parsed Authorization header
2425 struct ah {
2426  char *user, *uri, *cnonce, *response, *qop, *nc, *nonce;
2427 };
2428 
2429 // Return 1 on success. Always initializes the ah structure.
2430 static int parse_auth_header(struct mg_connection *conn, char *buf,
2431  size_t buf_size, struct ah *ah) {
2432  char *name, *value, *s;
2433  const char *auth_header;
2434 
2435  (void) memset(ah, 0, sizeof(*ah));
2436  if ((auth_header = mg_get_header(conn, "Authorization")) == NULL ||
2437  mg_strncasecmp(auth_header, "Digest ", 7) != 0) {
2438  return 0;
2439  }
2440 
2441  // Make modifiable copy of the auth header
2442  (void) mg_strlcpy(buf, auth_header + 7, buf_size);
2443  s = buf;
2444 
2445  // Parse authorization header
2446  for (;;) {
2447  // Gobble initial spaces
2448  while (isspace(* (unsigned char *) s)) {
2449  s++;
2450  }
2451  name = skip_quoted(&s, "=", " ", 0);
2452  // Value is either quote-delimited, or ends at first comma or space.
2453  if (s[0] == '\"') {
2454  s++;
2455  value = skip_quoted(&s, "\"", " ", '\\');
2456  if (s[0] == ',') {
2457  s++;
2458  }
2459  } else {
2460  value = skip_quoted(&s, ", ", " ", 0); // IE uses commas, FF uses spaces
2461  }
2462  if (*name == '\0') {
2463  break;
2464  }
2465 
2466  if (!strcmp(name, "username")) {
2467  ah->user = value;
2468  } else if (!strcmp(name, "cnonce")) {
2469  ah->cnonce = value;
2470  } else if (!strcmp(name, "response")) {
2471  ah->response = value;
2472  } else if (!strcmp(name, "uri")) {
2473  ah->uri = value;
2474  } else if (!strcmp(name, "qop")) {
2475  ah->qop = value;
2476  } else if (!strcmp(name, "nc")) {
2477  ah->nc = value;
2478  } else if (!strcmp(name, "nonce")) {
2479  ah->nonce = value;
2480  }
2481  }
2482 
2483  // CGI needs it as REMOTE_USER
2484  if (ah->user != NULL) {
2485  conn->request_info.remote_user = mg_strdup(ah->user);
2486  } else {
2487  return 0;
2488  }
2489 
2490  return 1;
2491 }
2492 
2493 static char *mg_fgets(char *buf, size_t size, struct file *filep, char **p) {
2494  char *eof;
2495  size_t len;
2496  char *memend;
2497 
2498  if (filep->membuf != NULL && *p != NULL) {
2499  memend = (char *) &filep->membuf[filep->size];
2500  eof = (char *) memchr(*p, '\n', memend - *p); // Search for \n from p till the end of stream
2501  if (eof != NULL) {
2502  eof += 1; // Include \n
2503  } else {
2504  eof = memend; // Copy remaining data
2505  }
2506  len = (size_t) (eof - *p) > size - 1 ? size - 1 : (size_t) (eof - *p);
2507  memcpy(buf, *p, len);
2508  buf[len] = '\0';
2509  *p += len;
2510  return len ? eof : NULL;
2511  } else if (filep->fp != NULL) {
2512  return fgets(buf, size, filep->fp);
2513  } else {
2514  return NULL;
2515  }
2516 }
2517 
2518 // Authorize against the opened passwords file. Return 1 if authorized.
2519 static int authorize(struct mg_connection *conn, struct file *filep) {
2520  struct ah ah;
2521  char line[256], f_user[256], ha1[256], f_domain[256], buf[MG_BUF_LEN], *p;
2522 
2523  if (!parse_auth_header(conn, buf, sizeof(buf), &ah)) {
2524  return 0;
2525  }
2526 
2527  // Loop over passwords file
2528  p = (char *) filep->membuf;
2529  while (mg_fgets(line, sizeof(line), filep, &p) != NULL) {
2530  if (sscanf(line, "%[^:]:%[^:]:%s", f_user, f_domain, ha1) != 3) {
2531  continue;
2532  }
2533 
2534  if (!strcmp(ah.user, f_user) &&
2535  !strcmp(conn->ctx->config[AUTHENTICATION_DOMAIN], f_domain))
2536  return check_password(conn->request_info.request_method, ha1, ah.uri,
2537  ah.nonce, ah.nc, ah.cnonce, ah.qop, ah.response);
2538  }
2539 
2540  return 0;
2541 }
2542 
2543 // Return 1 if request is authorised, 0 otherwise.
2544 static int check_authorization(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path) {
2545  char fname[PATH_MAX];
2546  struct vec uri_vec, filename_vec;
2547  const char *list;
2548  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
2549  int authorized = 1;
2550 
2551  list = conn->ctx->config[PROTECT_URI];
2552  while ((list = next_option(list, &uri_vec, &filename_vec)) != NULL) {
2553  if (!memcmp(conn->request_info.uri, uri_vec.ptr, uri_vec.len)) {
2554  mg_snprintf(conn, fname, sizeof(fname), "%.*s",
2555  (int) filename_vec.len, filename_vec.ptr);
2556  if (!mg_fopen(conn, fname, "r", &file)) {
2557  cry(conn, "%s: cannot open %s: %s", __func__, fname, strerror(errno));
2558  }
2559  break;
2560  }
2561  }
2562 
2563  if (!is_file_opened(&file)) {
2564  open_auth_file(conn, path, &file);
2565  }
2566 
2567  if (is_file_opened(&file)) {
2568  authorized = authorize(conn, &file);
2569  mg_fclose(&file);
2570  }
2571 
2572  return authorized;
2573 }

2575 static void send_authorization_request(struct mg_connection *conn) {

2581  "realm=\"%s\", nonce=\"%lu\"\r\n\r\n",
2582  conn->ctx->config[AUTHENTICATION_DOMAIN],
2583  (unsigned long) time(NULL));

2586 static int is_authorized_for_put(struct mg_connection *conn) {

2599 int mg_modify_passwords_file(const char *fname, const char *domain,
2600  const char *user, const char *pass) {
2601  int found;
2602  char line[512], u[512], d[512], ha1[33], tmp[PATH_MAX];
2603  FILE *fp, *fp2;
2604 
2605  found = 0;
2606  fp = fp2 = NULL;
2607 
2608  // Regard empty password as no password - remove user record.
2609  if (pass != NULL && pass[0] == '\0') {
2610  pass = NULL;
2611  }
2612 
2613  (void) snprintf(tmp, sizeof(tmp), "%s.tmp", fname);
2614 
2615  // Create the file if does not exist
2616  if ((fp = fopen(fname, "a+")) != NULL) {
2617  (void) fclose(fp);
2618  }
2619 
2620  // Open the given file and temporary file
2621  if ((fp = fopen(fname, "r")) == NULL) {
2622  return 0;
2623  } else if ((fp2 = fopen(tmp, "w+")) == NULL) {
2624  fclose(fp);
2625  return 0;
2626  }
2627 
2628  // Copy the stuff to temporary file
2629  while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), fp) != NULL) {
2630  if (sscanf(line, "%[^:]:%[^:]:%*s", u, d) != 2) {
2631  continue;
2632  }
2633 
2634  if (!strcmp(u, user) && !strcmp(d, domain)) {
2635  found++;
2636  if (pass != NULL) {
2637  mg_md5(ha1, user, ":", domain, ":", pass, NULL);
2638  fprintf(fp2, "%s:%s:%s\n", user, domain, ha1);
2639  }
2640  } else {
2641  fprintf(fp2, "%s", line);
2642  }
2643  }
2644 
2645  // If new user, just add it
2646  if (!found && pass != NULL) {
2647  mg_md5(ha1, user, ":", domain, ":", pass, NULL);
2648  fprintf(fp2, "%s:%s:%s\n", user, domain, ha1);
2649  }
2650 
2651  // Close files
2652  fclose(fp);
2653  fclose(fp2);
2654 
2655  // Put the temp file in place of real file
2656  remove(fname);
2657  rename(tmp, fname);
2658 
2659  return 1;
2660 }

2662 static SOCKET conn2(const char *host, int port, int use_ssl,
2663  char *ebuf, size_t ebuf_len) {
2664  struct sockaddr_in sin;
2665  struct hostent *he;
2666  SOCKET sock = INVALID_SOCKET;
2667 
2668  if (host == NULL) {
2669  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "%s", "NULL host");
2670  } else if (use_ssl && SSLv23_client_method == NULL) {
2671  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "%s", "SSL is not initialized");
2672  // TODO(lsm): use something threadsafe instead of gethostbyname()
2673  } else if ((he = gethostbyname(host)) == NULL) {
2674  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "gethostbyname(%s): %s", host, strerror(ERRNO));
2675  } else if ((sock = socket(PF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0)) == INVALID_SOCKET) {
2676  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "socket(): %s", strerror(ERRNO));
2677  } else {
2678  set_close_on_exec(sock);
2679  sin.sin_family = AF_INET;
2680  sin.sin_port = htons((uint16_t) port);
2681  sin.sin_addr = * (struct in_addr *) he->h_addr_list[0];
2682  if (connect(sock, (struct sockaddr *) &sin, sizeof(sin)) != 0) {
2683  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "connect(%s:%d): %s",
2684  host, port, strerror(ERRNO));
2685  closesocket(sock);
2686  sock = INVALID_SOCKET;
2687  }
2688  }
2689  return sock;
2690 }

2694 static void mg_url_encode(const char *src, char *dst, size_t dst_len) {
2695  static const char *dont_escape = "._-$,;~()";
2696  static const char *hex = "0123456789abcdef";
2697  const char *end = dst + dst_len - 1;
2698 
2699  for (; *src != '\0' && dst < end; src++, dst++) {
2700  if (isalnum(*(const unsigned char *) src) ||
2701  strchr(dont_escape, * (const unsigned char *) src) != NULL) {
2702  *dst = *src;
2703  } else if (dst + 2 < end) {
2704  dst[0] = '%';
2705  dst[1] = hex[(* (const unsigned char *) src) >> 4];
2706  dst[2] = hex[(* (const unsigned char *) src) & 0xf];
2707  dst += 2;
2708  }
2709  }
2710 
2711  *dst = '\0';
2712 }

2714 static void print_dir_entry(struct de *de) {
2715  char size[64], mod[64], href[PATH_MAX];
2716 
2717  if (de->file.is_directory) {
2718  mg_snprintf(de->conn, size, sizeof(size), "%s", "[DIRECTORY]");
2719  } else {
2720  // We use (signed) cast below because MSVC 6 compiler cannot
2721  // convert unsigned __int64 to double. Sigh.
2722  if (de->file.size < 1024) {
2723  mg_snprintf(de->conn, size, sizeof(size), "%d", (int) de->file.size);
2724  } else if (de->file.size < 0x100000) {
2725  mg_snprintf(de->conn, size, sizeof(size),
2726  "%.1fk", (double) de->file.size / 1024.0);
2727  } else if (de->file.size < 0x40000000) {
2728  mg_snprintf(de->conn, size, sizeof(size),
2729  "%.1fM", (double) de->file.size / 1048576);
2730  } else {
2731  mg_snprintf(de->conn, size, sizeof(size),
2732  "%.1fG", (double) de->file.size / 1073741824);
2733  }
2734  }
2735  strftime(mod, sizeof(mod), "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M",
2736  localtime(&de->file.modification_time));
2737  mg_url_encode(de->file_name, href, sizeof(href));
2738  de->conn->num_bytes_sent += mg_printf(de->conn,
2739  "<tr><td><a href=\"%s%s%s\">%s%s</a></td>"
2740  "<td>&nbsp;%s</td><td>&nbsp;&nbsp;%s</td></tr>\n",
2741  de->conn->request_info.uri, href, de->file.is_directory ? "/" : "",
2742  de->file_name, de->file.is_directory ? "/" : "", mod, size);
2743 }

2745 // This function is called from send_directory() and used for
2746 // sorting directory entries by size, or name, or modification time.
2747 // On windows, __cdecl specification is needed in case if project is built
2748 // with __stdcall convention. qsort always requires __cdels callback.
2749 static int WINCDECL compare_dir_entries(const void *p1, const void *p2) {
2750  const struct de *a = (const struct de *) p1, *b = (const struct de *) p2;
2751  const char *query_string = a->conn->request_info.query_string;
2752  int cmp_result = 0;
2753 
2754  if (query_string == NULL) {
2755  query_string = "na";
2756  }
2757 
2758  if (a->file.is_directory && !b->file.is_directory) {
2759  return -1; // Always put directories on top
2760  } else if (!a->file.is_directory && b->file.is_directory) {
2761  return 1; // Always put directories on top
2762  } else if (*query_string == 'n') {
2763  cmp_result = strcmp(a->file_name, b->file_name);
2764  } else if (*query_string == 's') {
2765  cmp_result = a->file.size == b->file.size ? 0 :
2766  a->file.size > b->file.size ? 1 : -1;
2767  } else if (*query_string == 'd') {
2768  cmp_result = a->file.modification_time == b->file.modification_time ? 0 :
2769  a->file.modification_time > b->file.modification_time ? 1 : -1;
2770  }
2771 
2772  return query_string[1] == 'd' ? -cmp_result : cmp_result;
2773 }

2775 static int must_hide_file(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path) {
2776  const char *pw_pattern = "**" PASSWORDS_FILE_NAME "$";
2777  const char *pattern = conn->ctx->config[HIDE_FILES];
2778  return match_prefix(pw_pattern, strlen(pw_pattern), path) > 0 ||
2779  (pattern != NULL && match_prefix(pattern, strlen(pattern), path) > 0);
2780 }

2782 static int scan_directory(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *dir,
2783  void *data, void (*cb)(struct de *, void *)) {
2784  char path[PATH_MAX];
2785  struct dirent *dp;
2786  DIR *dirp;
2787  struct de de;
2788 
2789  if ((dirp = opendir(dir)) == NULL) {
2790  return 0;
2791  } else {
2792  de.conn = conn;
2793 
2794  while ((dp = readdir(dirp)) != NULL) {
2795  // Do not show current dir and hidden files
2796  if (!strcmp(dp->d_name, ".") ||
2797  !strcmp(dp->d_name, "..") ||
2798  must_hide_file(conn, dp->d_name)) {
2799  continue;
2800  }
2801 
2802  mg_snprintf(conn, path, sizeof(path), "%s%c%s", dir, '/', dp->d_name);
2803 
2804  // If we don't memset stat structure to zero, mtime will have
2805  // garbage and strftime() will segfault later on in
2806  // print_dir_entry(). memset is required only if mg_stat()
2807  // fails. For more details, see
2808  // http://code.google.com/p/mongoose/issues/detail?id=79
2809  memset(&de.file, 0, sizeof(de.file));
2810  mg_stat(conn, path, &de.file);
2811 
2812  de.file_name = dp->d_name;
2813  cb(&de, data);
2814  }
2815  (void) closedir(dirp);
2816  }
2817  return 1;
2818 }

2820 static int remove_directory(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *dir) {
2821  char path[PATH_MAX];
2822  struct dirent *dp;
2823  DIR *dirp;
2824  struct de de;
2825 
2826  if ((dirp = opendir(dir)) == NULL) {
2827  return 0;
2828  } else {
2829  de.conn = conn;
2830 
2831  while ((dp = readdir(dirp)) != NULL) {
2832  // Do not show current dir (but show hidden files as they will also be removed)
2833  if (!strcmp(dp->d_name, ".") ||
2834  !strcmp(dp->d_name, "..")) {
2835  continue;
2836  }
2837 
2838  mg_snprintf(conn, path, sizeof(path), "%s%c%s", dir, '/', dp->d_name);
2839 
2840  // If we don't memset stat structure to zero, mtime will have
2841  // garbage and strftime() will segfault later on in
2842  // print_dir_entry(). memset is required only if mg_stat()
2843  // fails. For more details, see
2844  // http://code.google.com/p/mongoose/issues/detail?id=79
2845  memset(&de.file, 0, sizeof(de.file));
2846  mg_stat(conn, path, &de.file);
2847  if(de.file.modification_time) {
2848  if(de.file.is_directory) {
2849  remove_directory(conn, path);
2850  } else {
2851  mg_remove(path);
2852  }
2853  }
2854 
2855  }
2856  (void) closedir(dirp);
2857 
2858  rmdir(dir);
2859  }
2860 
2861  return 1;
2862 }

2870 // Behaves like realloc(), but frees original pointer on failure
2871 static void *realloc2(void *ptr, size_t size) {
2872  void *new_ptr = realloc(ptr, size);
2873  if (new_ptr == NULL) {
2874  free(ptr);
2875  }
2876  return new_ptr;
2877 }

2879 static void dir_scan_callback(struct de *de, void *data) {

2926  conn->request_info.uri, conn->request_info.uri,

2948 // Send len bytes from the opened file to the client.
2949 static void send_file_data(struct mg_connection *conn, struct file *filep,
2950  int64_t offset, int64_t len) {
2951  char buf[MG_BUF_LEN];
2952  int to_read, num_read, num_written;
2953 
2954  // Sanity check the offset
2955  offset = offset < 0 ? 0 : offset > filep->size ? filep->size : offset;
2956 
2957  if (len > 0 && filep->membuf != NULL && filep->size > 0) {
2958  if (len > filep->size - offset) {
2959  len = filep->size - offset;
2960  }
2961  mg_write(conn, filep->membuf + offset, (size_t) len);
2962  } else if (len > 0 && filep->fp != NULL) {
2963  fseeko(filep->fp, offset, SEEK_SET);
2964  while (len > 0) {
2965  // Calculate how much to read from the file in the buffer
2966  to_read = sizeof(buf);
2967  if ((int64_t) to_read > len) {
2968  to_read = (int) len;
2969  }
2970 
2971  // Read from file, exit the loop on error
2972  if ((num_read = fread(buf, 1, (size_t) to_read, filep->fp)) <= 0) {
2973  break;
2974  }
2975 
2976  // Send read bytes to the client, exit the loop on error
2977  if ((num_written = mg_write(conn, buf, (size_t) num_read)) != num_read) {
2978  break;
2979  }
2980 
2981  // Both read and were successful, adjust counters
2982  conn->num_bytes_sent += num_written;
2983  len -= num_written;
2984  }
2985  }
2986 }

3000  conn->ctx->callbacks.http_etag(conn, path, buf, buf_len)) {
3001  }

3016 static void handle_file_request(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path,
3017  struct file *filep) {
3018  char date[64], lm[64], etag[64], range[64];
3019  const char *msg = "OK", *hdr;
3020  time_t curtime = time(NULL);
3021  int64_t cl, r1, r2;
3022  struct vec mime_vec;
3023  int n;
3024  char gz_path[PATH_MAX];
3025  char const* encoding = "";
3026 
3027  get_mime_type(conn->ctx, path, &mime_vec);
3028  cl = filep->size;
3029  conn->status_code = 200;
3030  range[0] = '\0';
3031 
3032  // if this file is in fact a pre-gzipped file, rewrite its filename
3033  // it's important to rewrite the filename after resolving
3034  // the mime type from it, to preserve the actual file's type
3035  if (filep->gzipped) {
3036  snprintf(gz_path, sizeof(gz_path), "%s.gz", path);
3037  path = gz_path;
3038  encoding = "Content-Encoding: gzip\r\n";
3039  }
3040 
3041  if (!mg_fopen(conn, path, "rb", filep)) {
3042  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error,
3043  "fopen(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3044  return;
3045  }
3046 
3047  fclose_on_exec(filep);
3048 
3049  // If Range: header specified, act accordingly
3050  r1 = r2 = 0;
3051  hdr = mg_get_header(conn, "Range");
3052  if (hdr != NULL && (n = parse_range_header(hdr, &r1, &r2)) > 0 &&
3053  r1 >= 0 && r2 >= 0) {
3054  // actually, range requests don't play well with a pre-gzipped
3055  // file (since the range is specified in the uncmpressed space)
3056  if (filep->gzipped) {
3057  send_http_error(conn, 501, "Not Implemented", "range requests in gzipped files are not supported");
3058  return;
3059  }
3060  conn->status_code = 206;
3061  cl = n == 2 ? (r2 > cl ? cl : r2) - r1 + 1: cl - r1;
3062  mg_snprintf(conn, range, sizeof(range),
3063  "Content-Range: bytes "
3064  "%" INT64_FMT "-%"
3065  INT64_FMT "/%" INT64_FMT "\r\n",
3066  r1, r1 + cl - 1, filep->size);
3067  msg = "Partial Content";
3068  }
3069 
3070  // Prepare Etag, Date, Last-Modified headers. Must be in UTC, according to
3071  // http://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec3.html#sec3.3
3072  gmt_time_string(date, sizeof(date), &curtime);
3073  gmt_time_string(lm, sizeof(lm), &filep->modification_time);
3074  construct_etag(conn, path, etag, sizeof(etag), filep);
3075 
3076  (void) mg_printf(conn,
3077  "HTTP/1.1 %d %s\r\n"
3078  "Date: %s\r\n"
3079  "Last-Modified: %s\r\n"
3080  "Etag: %s\r\n"
3081  "Content-Type: %.*s\r\n"
3082  "Content-Length: %" INT64_FMT "\r\n"
3083  "Connection: %s\r\n"
3084  "Accept-Ranges: bytes\r\n"
3085  "%s%s\r\n",
3086  conn->status_code, msg, date, lm, etag, (int) mime_vec.len,
3087  mime_vec.ptr, cl, suggest_connection_header(conn), range, encoding);
3088 
3089  if (strcmp(conn->request_info.request_method, "HEAD") != 0) {
3090  send_file_data(conn, filep, r1, cl);
3091  }
3092  mg_fclose(filep);
3093 }

3105 // Parse HTTP headers from the given buffer, advance buffer to the point
3106 // where parsing stopped.
3107 static void parse_http_headers(char **buf, struct mg_request_info *ri) {
3108  int i;
3109 
3110  for (i = 0; i < (int) ARRAY_SIZE(ri->http_headers); i++) {
3111  ri->http_headers[i].name = skip_quoted(buf, ":", " ", 0);
3112  ri->http_headers[i].value = skip(buf, "\r\n");
3113  if (ri->http_headers[i].name[0] == '\0')
3114  break;
3115  ri->num_headers = i + 1;
3116  }
3117 }

3119 static int is_valid_http_method(const char *method) {
3120  return !strcmp(method, "GET") || !strcmp(method, "POST") ||
3121  !strcmp(method, "HEAD") || !strcmp(method, "CONNECT") ||
3122  !strcmp(method, "PUT") || !strcmp(method, "DELETE") ||
3123  !strcmp(method, "OPTIONS") || !strcmp(method, "PROPFIND")
3124  || !strcmp(method, "MKCOL")
3125  ;
3126 }
3127 
3128 // Parse HTTP request, fill in mg_request_info structure.
3129 // This function modifies the buffer by NUL-terminating
3130 // HTTP request components, header names and header values.
3131 static int parse_http_message(char *buf, int len, struct mg_request_info *ri) {
3132  int is_request, request_length = get_request_len(buf, len);
3133  if (request_length > 0) {
3134  // Reset attributes. DO NOT TOUCH is_ssl, remote_ip, remote_port
3135  ri->remote_user = ri->request_method = ri->uri = ri->http_version = NULL;
3136  ri->num_headers = 0;
3137 
3138  buf[request_length - 1] = '\0';
3139 
3140  // RFC says that all initial whitespaces should be ingored
3141  while (*buf != '\0' && isspace(* (unsigned char *) buf)) {
3142  buf++;
3143  }
3144  ri->request_method = skip(&buf, " ");
3145  ri->uri = skip(&buf, " ");
3146  ri->http_version = skip(&buf, "\r\n");
3147 
3148  // HTTP message could be either HTTP request or HTTP response, e.g.
3149  // "GET / HTTP/1.0 ...." or "HTTP/1.0 200 OK ..."
3150  is_request = is_valid_http_method(ri->request_method);
3151  if ((is_request && memcmp(ri->http_version, "HTTP/", 5) != 0) ||
3152  (!is_request && memcmp(ri->request_method, "HTTP/", 5) != 0)) {
3153  request_length = -1;
3154  } else {
3155  if (is_request) {
3156  ri->http_version += 5;
3157  }
3158  parse_http_headers(&buf, ri);
3159  }
3160  }
3161  return request_length;
3162 }
3163 
3164 // Keep reading the input (either opened file descriptor fd, or socket sock,
3165 // or SSL descriptor ssl) into buffer buf, until \r\n\r\n appears in the
3166 // buffer (which marks the end of HTTP request). Buffer buf may already
3167 // have some data. The length of the data is stored in nread.
3168 // Upon every read operation, increase nread by the number of bytes read.
3169 static int read_request(FILE *fp, struct mg_connection *conn,
3170  char *buf, int bufsiz, int *nread) {
3171  int request_len, n = 0;
3172 
3173  request_len = get_request_len(buf, *nread);
3174  while (conn->ctx->stop_flag == 0 &&
3175  *nread < bufsiz && request_len == 0 &&
3176  (n = pull(fp, conn, buf + *nread, bufsiz - *nread)) > 0) {
3177  *nread += n;
3178  assert(*nread <= bufsiz);
3179  request_len = get_request_len(buf, *nread);
3180  }
3181 
3182  return request_len <= 0 && n <= 0 ? -1 : request_len;
3183 }

3185 // For given directory path, substitute it to valid index file.
3186 // Return 0 if index file has been found, -1 if not found.
3187 // If the file is found, it's stats is returned in stp.
3188 static int substitute_index_file(struct mg_connection *conn, char *path,
3189  size_t path_len, struct file *filep) {
3190  const char *list = conn->ctx->config[INDEX_FILES];
3191  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
3192  struct vec filename_vec;
3193  size_t n = strlen(path);
3194  int found = 0;
3195 
3196  // The 'path' given to us points to the directory. Remove all trailing
3197  // directory separator characters from the end of the path, and
3198  // then append single directory separator character.
3199  while (n > 0 && path[n - 1] == '/') {
3200  n--;
3201  }
3202  path[n] = '/';
3203 
3204  // Traverse index files list. For each entry, append it to the given
3205  // path and see if the file exists. If it exists, break the loop
3206  while ((list = next_option(list, &filename_vec, NULL)) != NULL) {
3207 
3208  // Ignore too long entries that may overflow path buffer
3209  if (filename_vec.len > path_len - (n + 2))
3210  continue;
3211 
3212  // Prepare full path to the index file
3213  mg_strlcpy(path + n + 1, filename_vec.ptr, filename_vec.len + 1);
3214 
3215  // Does it exist?
3216  if (mg_stat(conn, path, &file)) {
3217  // Yes it does, break the loop
3218  *filep = file;
3219  found = 1;
3220  break;
3221  }
3222  }
3223 
3224  // If no index file exists, restore directory path
3225  if (!found) {
3226  path[n] = '\0';
3227  }
3228 
3229  return found;
3230 }

3232 // Return True if we should reply 304 Not Modified.
3233 static int is_not_modified(const struct mg_connection *conn,
3234  const char *path,
3235  const struct file *filep) {
3236  char etag[64];
3237  const char *ims = mg_get_header(conn, "If-Modified-Since");
3238  const char *inm = mg_get_header(conn, "If-None-Match");
3239  construct_etag(conn, path, etag, sizeof(etag), filep);

3241  (ims != NULL && filep->modification_time <= parse_date_string(ims));

3244 static int forward_body_data(struct mg_connection *conn, FILE *fp,
3245  SOCKET sock, SSL *ssl) {
3246  const char *expect, *body;
3247  char buf[MG_BUF_LEN];
3248  int to_read, nread, buffered_len, success = 0;
3249 
3250  expect = mg_get_header(conn, "Expect");
3251  assert(fp != NULL);
3252 
3253  if (conn->content_len == -1) {
3254  send_http_error(conn, 411, "Length Required", "%s", "");
3255  } else if (expect != NULL && mg_strcasecmp(expect, "100-continue")) {
3256  send_http_error(conn, 417, "Expectation Failed", "%s", "");
3257  } else {
3258  if (expect != NULL) {
3259  (void) mg_printf(conn, "%s", "HTTP/1.1 100 Continue\r\n\r\n");
3260  }
3261 
3262  body = conn->buf + conn->request_len + conn->consumed_content;
3263  buffered_len = &conn->buf[conn->data_len] - body;
3264  assert(buffered_len >= 0);
3265  assert(conn->consumed_content == 0);
3266 
3267  if (buffered_len > 0) {
3268  if ((int64_t) buffered_len > conn->content_len) {
3269  buffered_len = (int) conn->content_len;
3270  }
3271  push(fp, sock, ssl, body, (int64_t) buffered_len);
3272  conn->consumed_content += buffered_len;
3273  }
3274 
3275  nread = 0;
3276  while (conn->consumed_content < conn->content_len) {
3277  to_read = sizeof(buf);
3278  if ((int64_t) to_read > conn->content_len - conn->consumed_content) {
3279  to_read = (int) (conn->content_len - conn->consumed_content);
3280  }
3281  nread = pull(NULL, conn, buf, to_read);
3282  if (nread <= 0 || push(fp, sock, ssl, buf, nread) != nread) {
3283  break;
3284  }
3285  conn->consumed_content += nread;
3286  }
3287 
3288  if (conn->consumed_content == conn->content_len) {
3289  success = nread >= 0;
3290  }
3291 
3292  // Each error code path in this function must send an error
3293  if (!success) {
3294  send_http_error(conn, 577, http_500_error, "%s", "");
3295  }
3296  }
3297 
3298  return success;
3299 }

3301 #if !defined(NO_CGI)
3302 // This structure helps to create an environment for the spawned CGI program.
3303 // Environment is an array of "VARIABLE=VALUE\0" ASCIIZ strings,
3304 // last element must be NULL.
3305 // However, on Windows there is a requirement that all these VARIABLE=VALUE\0
3306 // strings must reside in a contiguous buffer. The end of the buffer is
3307 // marked by two '\0' characters.
3308 // We satisfy both worlds: we create an envp array (which is vars), all
3309 // entries are actually pointers inside buf.
3310 struct cgi_env_block {
3311  struct mg_connection *conn;
3312  char buf[CGI_ENVIRONMENT_SIZE]; // Environment buffer
3313  int len; // Space taken
3314  char *vars[MAX_CGI_ENVIR_VARS]; // char **envp
3315  int nvars; // Number of variables
3316 };
3317 
3318 static char *addenv(struct cgi_env_block *block,
3319  PRINTF_FORMAT_STRING(const char *fmt), ...)
3320  PRINTF_ARGS(2, 3);
3321 
3322 // Append VARIABLE=VALUE\0 string to the buffer, and add a respective
3323 // pointer into the vars array.
3324 static char *addenv(struct cgi_env_block *block, const char *fmt, ...) {
3325  int n, space;
3326  char *added;
3327  va_list ap;
3328 
3329  // Calculate how much space is left in the buffer
3330  space = sizeof(block->buf) - block->len - 2;
3331  assert(space >= 0);
3332 
3333  // Make a pointer to the free space int the buffer
3334  added = block->buf + block->len;
3335 
3336  // Copy VARIABLE=VALUE\0 string into the free space
3337  va_start(ap, fmt);
3338  n = mg_vsnprintf(block->conn, added, (size_t) space, fmt, ap);
3339  va_end(ap);
3340 
3341  // Make sure we do not overflow buffer and the envp array
3342  if (n > 0 && n + 1 < space &&
3343  block->nvars < (int) ARRAY_SIZE(block->vars) - 2) {
3344  // Append a pointer to the added string into the envp array
3345  block->vars[block->nvars++] = added;
3346  // Bump up used length counter. Include \0 terminator
3347  block->len += n + 1;
3348  } else {
3349  cry(block->conn, "%s: CGI env buffer truncated for [%s]", __func__, fmt);
3350  }
3351 
3352  return added;
3353 }

3355 static void prepare_cgi_environment(struct mg_connection *conn,
3356  const char *prog,
3357  struct cgi_env_block *blk) {
3358  const char *s, *slash;
3359  struct vec var_vec;
3360  char *p, src_addr[IP_ADDR_STR_LEN];
3361  int i;
3362 
3363  blk->len = blk->nvars = 0;
3364  blk->conn = conn;
3365  sockaddr_to_string(src_addr, sizeof(src_addr), &conn->client.rsa);
3366 
3367  addenv(blk, "SERVER_NAME=%s", conn->ctx->config[AUTHENTICATION_DOMAIN]);
3368  addenv(blk, "SERVER_ROOT=%s", conn->ctx->config[DOCUMENT_ROOT]);
3369  addenv(blk, "DOCUMENT_ROOT=%s", conn->ctx->config[DOCUMENT_ROOT]);
3370  addenv(blk, "SERVER_SOFTWARE=%s/%s", "Mongoose", mg_version());
3371 
3372  // Prepare the environment block
3373  addenv(blk, "%s", "GATEWAY_INTERFACE=CGI/1.1");
3374  addenv(blk, "%s", "SERVER_PROTOCOL=HTTP/1.1");
3375  addenv(blk, "%s", "REDIRECT_STATUS=200"); // For PHP
3376 
3377  // TODO(lsm): fix this for IPv6 case
3378  addenv(blk, "SERVER_PORT=%d", ntohs(conn->client.lsa.sin.sin_port));
3379 
3380  addenv(blk, "REQUEST_METHOD=%s", conn->request_info.request_method);
3381  addenv(blk, "REMOTE_ADDR=%s", src_addr);
3382  addenv(blk, "REMOTE_PORT=%d", conn->request_info.remote_port);
3383  addenv(blk, "REQUEST_URI=%s", conn->request_info.uri);
3384 
3385  // SCRIPT_NAME
3386  assert(conn->request_info.uri[0] == '/');
3387  slash = strrchr(conn->request_info.uri, '/');
3388  if ((s = strrchr(prog, '/')) == NULL)
3389  s = prog;
3390  addenv(blk, "SCRIPT_NAME=%.*s%s", (int) (slash - conn->request_info.uri),
3391  conn->request_info.uri, s);
3392 
3393  addenv(blk, "SCRIPT_FILENAME=%s", prog);
3394  addenv(blk, "PATH_TRANSLATED=%s", prog);
3395  addenv(blk, "HTTPS=%s", conn->ssl == NULL ? "off" : "on");
3396 
3397  if ((s = mg_get_header(conn, "Content-Type")) != NULL)
3398  addenv(blk, "CONTENT_TYPE=%s", s);
3399 
3400  if (conn->request_info.query_string != NULL)
3401  addenv(blk, "QUERY_STRING=%s", conn->request_info.query_string);
3402 
3403  if ((s = mg_get_header(conn, "Content-Length")) != NULL)
3404  addenv(blk, "CONTENT_LENGTH=%s", s);
3405 
3406  if ((s = getenv("PATH")) != NULL)
3407  addenv(blk, "PATH=%s", s);
3408 
3409  if (conn->path_info != NULL) {
3410  addenv(blk, "PATH_INFO=%s", conn->path_info);
3411  }
3412 
3413 #if defined(_WIN32)
3414  if ((s = getenv("COMSPEC")) != NULL) {
3415  addenv(blk, "COMSPEC=%s", s);
3416  }
3417  if ((s = getenv("SYSTEMROOT")) != NULL) {
3418  addenv(blk, "SYSTEMROOT=%s", s);
3419  }
3420  if ((s = getenv("SystemDrive")) != NULL) {
3421  addenv(blk, "SystemDrive=%s", s);
3422  }
3423  if ((s = getenv("ProgramFiles")) != NULL) {
3424  addenv(blk, "ProgramFiles=%s", s);
3425  }
3426  if ((s = getenv("ProgramFiles(x86)")) != NULL) {
3427  addenv(blk, "ProgramFiles(x86)=%s", s);
3428  }
3429 #else
3430  if ((s = getenv("LD_LIBRARY_PATH")) != NULL)
3431  addenv(blk, "LD_LIBRARY_PATH=%s", s);
3432 #endif // _WIN32
3433 
3434  if ((s = getenv("PERLLIB")) != NULL)
3435  addenv(blk, "PERLLIB=%s", s);
3436 
3437  if (conn->request_info.remote_user != NULL) {
3438  addenv(blk, "REMOTE_USER=%s", conn->request_info.remote_user);
3439  addenv(blk, "%s", "AUTH_TYPE=Digest");
3440  }
3441 
3442  // Add all headers as HTTP_* variables
3443  for (i = 0; i < conn->request_info.num_headers; i++) {
3444  p = addenv(blk, "HTTP_%s=%s",
3445  conn->request_info.http_headers[i].name,
3446  conn->request_info.http_headers[i].value);
3447 
3448  // Convert variable name into uppercase, and change - to _
3449  for (; *p != '=' && *p != '\0'; p++) {
3450  if (*p == '-')
3451  *p = '_';
3452  *p = (char) toupper(* (unsigned char *) p);
3453  }
3454  }
3455 
3456  // Add user-specified variables
3457  s = conn->ctx->config[CGI_ENVIRONMENT];
3458  while ((s = next_option(s, &var_vec, NULL)) != NULL) {
3459  addenv(blk, "%.*s", (int) var_vec.len, var_vec.ptr);
3460  }
3461 
3462  blk->vars[blk->nvars++] = NULL;
3463  blk->buf[blk->len++] = '\0';
3464 
3465  assert(blk->nvars < (int) ARRAY_SIZE(blk->vars));
3466  assert(blk->len > 0);
3467  assert(blk->len < (int) sizeof(blk->buf));
3468 }

3470 static void handle_cgi_request(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *prog) {
3471  int headers_len, data_len, i, fdin[2], fdout[2];
3472  const char *status, *status_text;
3473  char buf[16384], *pbuf, dir[PATH_MAX], *p;
3474  struct mg_request_info ri;
3475  struct cgi_env_block blk;
3476  FILE *in = NULL, *out = NULL;
3477  struct file fout = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
3478  pid_t pid = (pid_t) -1;
3479 
3480  prepare_cgi_environment(conn, prog, &blk);
3481 
3482  // CGI must be executed in its own directory. 'dir' must point to the
3483  // directory containing executable program, 'p' must point to the
3484  // executable program name relative to 'dir'.
3485  (void) mg_snprintf(conn, dir, sizeof(dir), "%s", prog);
3486  if ((p = strrchr(dir, '/')) != NULL) {
3487  *p++ = '\0';
3488  } else {
3489  dir[0] = '.', dir[1] = '\0';
3490  p = (char *) prog;
3491  }
3492 
3493  if (pipe(fdin) != 0 || pipe(fdout) != 0) {
3494  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error,
3495  "Cannot create CGI pipe: %s", strerror(ERRNO));
3496  goto done;
3497  }
3498 
3499  pid = spawn_process(conn, p, blk.buf, blk.vars, fdin[0], fdout[1], dir);
3500  if (pid == (pid_t) -1) {
3501  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error,
3502  "Cannot spawn CGI process [%s]: %s", prog, strerror(ERRNO));
3503  goto done;
3504  }
3505 
3506  // Make sure child closes all pipe descriptors. It must dup them to 0,1
3507  set_close_on_exec(fdin[0]);
3508  set_close_on_exec(fdin[1]);
3509  set_close_on_exec(fdout[0]);
3510  set_close_on_exec(fdout[1]);
3511 
3512  // Parent closes only one side of the pipes.
3513  // If we don't mark them as closed, close() attempt before
3514  // return from this function throws an exception on Windows.
3515  // Windows does not like when closed descriptor is closed again.
3516  (void) close(fdin[0]);
3517  (void) close(fdout[1]);
3518  fdin[0] = fdout[1] = -1;
3519 
3520 
3521  if ((in = fdopen(fdin[1], "wb")) == NULL ||
3522  (out = fdopen(fdout[0], "rb")) == NULL) {
3523  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error,
3524  "fopen: %s", strerror(ERRNO));
3525  goto done;
3526  }
3527 
3528  setbuf(in, NULL);
3529  setbuf(out, NULL);
3530  fout.fp = out;
3531 
3532  // Send POST data to the CGI process if needed
3533  if (!strcmp(conn->request_info.request_method, "POST") &&
3534  !forward_body_data(conn, in, INVALID_SOCKET, NULL)) {
3535  goto done;
3536  }
3537 
3538  // Close so child gets an EOF.
3539  fclose(in);
3540  in = NULL;
3541  fdin[1] = -1;
3542 
3543  // Now read CGI reply into a buffer. We need to set correct
3544  // status code, thus we need to see all HTTP headers first.
3545  // Do not send anything back to client, until we buffer in all
3546  // HTTP headers.
3547  data_len = 0;
3548  headers_len = read_request(out, conn, buf, sizeof(buf), &data_len);
3549  if (headers_len <= 0) {
3550  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error,
3551  "CGI program sent malformed or too big (>%u bytes) "
3552  "HTTP headers: [%.*s]",
3553  (unsigned) sizeof(buf), data_len, buf);
3554  goto done;
3555  }
3556  pbuf = buf;
3557  buf[headers_len - 1] = '\0';
3558  parse_http_headers(&pbuf, &ri);
3559 
3560  // Make up and send the status line
3561  status_text = "OK";
3562  if ((status = get_header(&ri, "Status")) != NULL) {
3563  conn->status_code = atoi(status);
3564  status_text = status;
3565  while (isdigit(* (unsigned char *) status_text) || *status_text == ' ') {
3566  status_text++;
3567  }
3568  } else if (get_header(&ri, "Location") != NULL) {
3569  conn->status_code = 302;
3570  } else {
3571  conn->status_code = 200;
3572  }
3573  if (get_header(&ri, "Connection") != NULL &&
3574  !mg_strcasecmp(get_header(&ri, "Connection"), "keep-alive")) {
3575  conn->must_close = 1;
3576  }
3577  (void) mg_printf(conn, "HTTP/1.1 %d %s\r\n", conn->status_code,
3578  status_text);
3579 
3580  // Send headers
3581  for (i = 0; i < ri.num_headers; i++) {
3582  mg_printf(conn, "%s: %s\r\n",
3583  ri.http_headers[i].name, ri.http_headers[i].value);
3584  }
3585  mg_write(conn, "\r\n", 2);
3586 
3587  // Send chunk of data that may have been read after the headers
3588  conn->num_bytes_sent += mg_write(conn, buf + headers_len,
3589  (size_t)(data_len - headers_len));
3590 
3591  // Read the rest of CGI output and send to the client
3592  send_file_data(conn, &fout, 0, INT64_MAX);
3593 
3594 done:
3595  if (pid != (pid_t) -1) {
3596  kill(pid, SIGKILL);
3597  }
3598  if (fdin[0] != -1) {
3599  close(fdin[0]);
3600  }
3601  if (fdout[1] != -1) {
3602  close(fdout[1]);
3603  }
3604 
3605  if (in != NULL) {
3606  fclose(in);
3607  } else if (fdin[1] != -1) {
3608  close(fdin[1]);
3609  }
3610 
3611  if (out != NULL) {
3612  fclose(out);
3613  } else if (fdout[0] != -1) {
3614  close(fdout[0]);
3615  }
3616 }
3617 #endif // !NO_CGI
3618 
3619 // For a given PUT path, create all intermediate subdirectories
3620 // for given path. Return 0 if the path itself is a directory,
3621 // or -1 on error, 1 if OK.
3622 static int put_dir(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path) {
3623  char buf[PATH_MAX];
3624  const char *s, *p;
3625  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
3626  int len, res = 1;
3627 
3628  for (s = p = path + 2; (p = strchr(s, '/')) != NULL; s = ++p) {
3629  len = p - path;
3630  if (len >= (int) sizeof(buf)) {
3631  res = -1;
3632  break;
3633  }
3634  memcpy(buf, path, len);
3635  buf[len] = '\0';
3636 
3637  // Try to create intermediate directory
3638  DEBUG_TRACE(("mkdir(%s)", buf));
3639  if (!mg_stat(conn, buf, &file) && mg_mkdir(buf, 0755) != 0) {
3640  res = -1;
3641  break;
3642  }
3643 
3644  // Is path itself a directory?
3645  if (p[1] == '\0') {
3646  res = 0;
3647  }
3648  }
3649 
3650  return res;
3651 }
3652 
3653 static void mkcol(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path) {
3654  int rc, body_len;
3655  struct de de;
3656  memset(&de.file, 0, sizeof(de.file));
3657  mg_stat(conn, path, &de.file);
3658 
3659  if(de.file.modification_time) {
3660  send_http_error(conn, 405, "Method Not Allowed",
3661  "mkcol(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3662  return;
3663  }
3664 
3665  body_len = conn->data_len - conn->request_len;
3666  if(body_len > 0) {
3667  send_http_error(conn, 415, "Unsupported media type",
3668  "mkcol(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3669  return;
3670  }
3671 
3672  rc = mg_mkdir(path, 0755);
3673 
3674  if (rc == 0) {
3675  conn->status_code = 201;
3676  mg_printf(conn, "HTTP/1.1 %d Created\r\n\r\n", conn->status_code);
3677  } else if (rc == -1) {
3678  if(errno == EEXIST)
3679  send_http_error(conn, 405, "Method Not Allowed",
3680  "mkcol(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3681  else if(errno == EACCES)
3682  send_http_error(conn, 403, "Forbidden",
3683  "mkcol(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3684  else if(errno == ENOENT)
3685  send_http_error(conn, 409, "Conflict",
3686  "mkcol(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3687  else
3688  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error,
3689  "fopen(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3690  }
3691 }

3693 static void put_file(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path) {
3694  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
3695  const char *range;
3696  int64_t r1, r2;
3697  int rc;
3698 
3699  conn->status_code = mg_stat(conn, path, &file) ? 200 : 201;
3700 
3701  if ((rc = put_dir(conn, path)) == 0) {
3702  mg_printf(conn, "HTTP/1.1 %d OK\r\n\r\n", conn->status_code);
3703  } else if (rc == -1) {
3704  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error,
3705  "put_dir(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3706  } else if (!mg_fopen(conn, path, "wb+", &file) || file.fp == NULL) {
3707  mg_fclose(&file);
3708  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error,
3709  "fopen(%s): %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
3710  } else {
3711  fclose_on_exec(&file);
3712  range = mg_get_header(conn, "Content-Range");
3713  r1 = r2 = 0;
3714  if (range != NULL && parse_range_header(range, &r1, &r2) > 0) {
3715  conn->status_code = 206;
3716  fseeko(file.fp, r1, SEEK_SET);
3717  }
3718  if (!forward_body_data(conn, file.fp, INVALID_SOCKET, NULL)) {
3719  conn->status_code = 500;
3720  }
3721  mg_printf(conn, "HTTP/1.1 %d OK\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n",
3722  conn->status_code);
3723  mg_fclose(&file);
3724  }
3725 }
