3727 static void send_ssi_file(struct mg_connection *, const char *,
3728  struct file *, int);
3729 
3730 static void do_ssi_include(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *ssi,
3731  char *tag, int include_level) {
3732  char file_name[MG_BUF_LEN], path[PATH_MAX], *p;
3733  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
3734 
3735  // sscanf() is safe here, since send_ssi_file() also uses buffer
3736  // of size MG_BUF_LEN to get the tag. So strlen(tag) is always < MG_BUF_LEN.
3737  if (sscanf(tag, " virtual=\"%[^\"]\"", file_name) == 1) {
3738  // File name is relative to the webserver root
3739  (void) mg_snprintf(conn, path, sizeof(path), "%s%c%s",
3740  conn->ctx->config[DOCUMENT_ROOT], '/', file_name);
3741  } else if (sscanf(tag, " abspath=\"%[^\"]\"", file_name) == 1) {
3742  // File name is relative to the webserver working directory
3743  // or it is absolute system path
3744  (void) mg_snprintf(conn, path, sizeof(path), "%s", file_name);
3745  } else if (sscanf(tag, " file=\"%[^\"]\"", file_name) == 1 ||
3746  sscanf(tag, " \"%[^\"]\"", file_name) == 1) {
3747  // File name is relative to the currect document
3748  (void) mg_snprintf(conn, path, sizeof(path), "%s", ssi);
3749  if ((p = strrchr(path, '/')) != NULL) {
3750  p[1] = '\0';
3751  }
3752  (void) mg_snprintf(conn, path + strlen(path),
3753  sizeof(path) - strlen(path), "%s", file_name);
3754  } else {
3755  cry(conn, "Bad SSI #include: [%s]", tag);
3756  return;
3757  }
3758 
3759  if (!mg_fopen(conn, path, "rb", &file)) {
3760  cry(conn, "Cannot open SSI #include: [%s]: fopen(%s): %s",
3761  tag, path, strerror(ERRNO));
3762  } else {
3763  fclose_on_exec(&file);
3764  if (match_prefix(conn->ctx->config[SSI_EXTENSIONS],
3765  strlen(conn->ctx->config[SSI_EXTENSIONS]), path) > 0) {
3766  send_ssi_file(conn, path, &file, include_level + 1);
3767  } else {
3768  send_file_data(conn, &file, 0, INT64_MAX);
3769  }
3770  mg_fclose(&file);
3771  }
3772 }

3774 #if !defined(NO_POPEN)
3775 static void do_ssi_exec(struct mg_connection *conn, char *tag) {
3776  char cmd[MG_BUF_LEN];
3777  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
3778 
3779  if (sscanf(tag, " \"%[^\"]\"", cmd) != 1) {
3780  cry(conn, "Bad SSI #exec: [%s]", tag);
3781  } else if ((file.fp = popen(cmd, "r")) == NULL) {
3782  cry(conn, "Cannot SSI #exec: [%s]: %s", cmd, strerror(ERRNO));
3783  } else {
3784  send_file_data(conn, &file, 0, INT64_MAX);
3785  pclose(file.fp);
3786  }
3787 }
3788 #endif // !NO_POPEN

3790 static int mg_fgetc(struct file *filep, int offset) {
3791  if (filep->membuf != NULL && offset >=0 && offset < filep->size) {
3792  return ((unsigned char *) filep->membuf)[offset];
3793  } else if (filep->fp != NULL) {
3794  return fgetc(filep->fp);
3795  } else {
3796  return EOF;
3797  }
3798 }
3799 
3800 static void send_ssi_file(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path,
3801  struct file *filep, int include_level) {
3802  char buf[MG_BUF_LEN];
3803  int ch, offset, len, in_ssi_tag;
3804 
3805  if (include_level > 10) {
3806  cry(conn, "SSI #include level is too deep (%s)", path);
3807  return;
3808  }
3809 
3810  in_ssi_tag = len = offset = 0;
3811  while ((ch = mg_fgetc(filep, offset)) != EOF) {
3812  if (in_ssi_tag && ch == '>') {
3813  in_ssi_tag = 0;
3814  buf[len++] = (char) ch;
3815  buf[len] = '\0';
3816  assert(len <= (int) sizeof(buf));
3817  if (len < 6 || memcmp(buf, "<!--#", 5) != 0) {
3818  // Not an SSI tag, pass it
3819  (void) mg_write(conn, buf, (size_t) len);
3820  } else {
3821  if (!memcmp(buf + 5, "include", 7)) {
3822  do_ssi_include(conn, path, buf + 12, include_level);
3823 #if !defined(NO_POPEN)
3824  } else if (!memcmp(buf + 5, "exec", 4)) {
3825  do_ssi_exec(conn, buf + 9);
3826 #endif // !NO_POPEN
3827  } else {
3828  cry(conn, "%s: unknown SSI " "command: \"%s\"", path, buf);
3829  }
3830  }
3831  len = 0;
3832  } else if (in_ssi_tag) {
3833  if (len == 5 && memcmp(buf, "<!--#", 5) != 0) {
3834  // Not an SSI tag
3835  in_ssi_tag = 0;
3836  } else if (len == (int) sizeof(buf) - 2) {
3837  cry(conn, "%s: SSI tag is too large", path);
3838  len = 0;
3839  }
3840  buf[len++] = ch & 0xff;
3841  } else if (ch == '<') {
3842  in_ssi_tag = 1;
3843  if (len > 0) {
3844  mg_write(conn, buf, (size_t) len);
3845  }
3846  len = 0;
3847  buf[len++] = ch & 0xff;
3848  } else {
3849  buf[len++] = ch & 0xff;
3850  if (len == (int) sizeof(buf)) {
3851  mg_write(conn, buf, (size_t) len);
3852  len = 0;
3853  }
3854  }
3855  }
3856 
3857  // Send the rest of buffered data
3858  if (len > 0) {
3859  mg_write(conn, buf, (size_t) len);
3860  }
3861 }

3863 static void handle_ssi_file_request(struct mg_connection *conn,
3864  const char *path) {
3865  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
3866 
3867  if (!mg_fopen(conn, path, "rb", &file)) {
3868  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error, "fopen(%s): %s", path,
3869  strerror(ERRNO));

3871  conn->must_close = 1;

3874  "Content-Type: text/html\r\nConnection: %s\r\n\r\n",
3875  suggest_connection_header(conn));
3876  send_ssi_file(conn, path, &file, 0);
3877  mg_fclose(&file);
3878  }

3922 static void handle_propfind(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *path,
3923  struct file *filep) {
3924  const char *depth = mg_get_header(conn, "Depth");
3925 
3926  conn->must_close = 1;

3928  mg_printf(conn, "HTTP/1.1 207 Multi-Status\r\n"
3929  "Connection: close\r\n"
3930  "Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8\r\n\r\n");

3932  conn->num_bytes_sent += mg_printf(conn,
3933  "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"?>"

3937  print_props(conn, conn->request_info.uri, filep);

3939  // If it is a directory, print directory entries too if Depth is not 0
3940  if (filep->is_directory &&
3941  !mg_strcasecmp(conn->ctx->config[ENABLE_DIRECTORY_LISTING], "yes") &&
3942  (depth == NULL || strcmp(depth, "0") != 0)) {
3943  scan_directory(conn, path, conn, &print_dav_dir_entry);
3944  }
3945 
3946  conn->num_bytes_sent += mg_printf(conn, "%s\n", "</d:multistatus>");

3951 // START OF SHA-1 code

3958 union char64long16 { unsigned char c[64]; uint32_t l[16]; };

3960 #define rol(value, bits) (((value) << (bits)) | ((value) >> (32 - (bits))))

3962 static uint32_t blk0(union char64long16 *block, int i) {

3964  if (!is_big_endian()) {

3966  (rol(block->l[i], 8) & 0x00FF00FF);

3972  ^block->l[(i+2)&15]^block->l[i&15],1))

3990  a = state[0];
3991  b = state[1];
3992  c = state[2];
3993  d = state[3];
3994  e = state[4];
3995  R0(a,b,c,d,e, 0); R0(e,a,b,c,d, 1); R0(d,e,a,b,c, 2); R0(c,d,e,a,b, 3);
3996  R0(b,c,d,e,a, 4); R0(a,b,c,d,e, 5); R0(e,a,b,c,d, 6); R0(d,e,a,b,c, 7);
3997  R0(c,d,e,a,b, 8); R0(b,c,d,e,a, 9); R0(a,b,c,d,e,10); R0(e,a,b,c,d,11);
3998  R0(d,e,a,b,c,12); R0(c,d,e,a,b,13); R0(b,c,d,e,a,14); R0(a,b,c,d,e,15);
3999  R1(e,a,b,c,d,16); R1(d,e,a,b,c,17); R1(c,d,e,a,b,18); R1(b,c,d,e,a,19);
4000  R2(a,b,c,d,e,20); R2(e,a,b,c,d,21); R2(d,e,a,b,c,22); R2(c,d,e,a,b,23);
4001  R2(b,c,d,e,a,24); R2(a,b,c,d,e,25); R2(e,a,b,c,d,26); R2(d,e,a,b,c,27);
4002  R2(c,d,e,a,b,28); R2(b,c,d,e,a,29); R2(a,b,c,d,e,30); R2(e,a,b,c,d,31);
4003  R2(d,e,a,b,c,32); R2(c,d,e,a,b,33); R2(b,c,d,e,a,34); R2(a,b,c,d,e,35);
4004  R2(e,a,b,c,d,36); R2(d,e,a,b,c,37); R2(c,d,e,a,b,38); R2(b,c,d,e,a,39);

4008  R3(d,e,a,b,c,52); R3(c,d,e,a,b,53); R3(b,c,d,e,a,54); R3(a,b,c,d,e,55);
4009  R3(e,a,b,c,d,56); R3(d,e,a,b,c,57); R3(c,d,e,a,b,58); R3(b,c,d,e,a,59);
4010  R4(a,b,c,d,e,60); R4(e,a,b,c,d,61); R4(d,e,a,b,c,62); R4(c,d,e,a,b,63);
4011  R4(b,c,d,e,a,64); R4(a,b,c,d,e,65); R4(e,a,b,c,d,66); R4(d,e,a,b,c,67);
4012  R4(c,d,e,a,b,68); R4(b,c,d,e,a,69); R4(a,b,c,d,e,70); R4(e,a,b,c,d,71);
4013  R4(d,e,a,b,c,72); R4(c,d,e,a,b,73); R4(b,c,d,e,a,74); R4(a,b,c,d,e,75);
4014  R4(e,a,b,c,d,76); R4(d,e,a,b,c,77); R4(c,d,e,a,b,78); R4(b,c,d,e,a,79);
4015  state[0] += a;
4016  state[1] += b;
4017  state[2] += c;
4018  state[3] += d;
4019  state[4] += e;
4020  a = b = c = d = e = 0;

4024 static void SHA1Init(SHA1_CTX* context) {
4025  context->state[0] = 0x67452301;
4026  context->state[1] = 0xEFCDAB89;
4027  context->state[2] = 0x98BADCFE;
4028  context->state[3] = 0x10325476;
4029  context->state[4] = 0xC3D2E1F0;
4030  context->count[0] = context->count[1] = 0;
4031 }
4032 
4033 static void SHA1Update(SHA1_CTX* context, const unsigned char* data,
4034  uint32_t len) {
4035  uint32_t i, j;
4036 
4037  j = context->count[0];
4038  if ((context->count[0] += len << 3) < j)
4039  context->count[1]++;
4040  context->count[1] += (len>>29);
4041  j = (j >> 3) & 63;
4042  if ((j + len) > 63) {
4043  memcpy(&context->buffer[j], data, (i = 64-j));
4044  SHA1Transform(context->state, context->buffer);
4045  for ( ; i + 63 < len; i += 64) {
4046  SHA1Transform(context->state, &data[i]);
4047  }
4048  j = 0;
4049  }
4050  else i = 0;
4051  memcpy(&context->buffer[j], &data[i], len - i);
4052 }
4053 
4054 static void SHA1Final(unsigned char digest[20], SHA1_CTX* context) {
4055  unsigned i;
4056  unsigned char finalcount[8], c;
4057 
4058  for (i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
4059  finalcount[i] = (unsigned char)((context->count[(i >= 4 ? 0 : 1)]
4060  >> ((3-(i & 3)) * 8) ) & 255);
4061  }
4062  c = 0200;
4063  SHA1Update(context, &c, 1);
4064  while ((context->count[0] & 504) != 448) {
4065  c = 0000;
4066  SHA1Update(context, &c, 1);
4067  }
4068  SHA1Update(context, finalcount, 8);
4069  for (i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
4070  digest[i] = (unsigned char)
4071  ((context->state[i>>2] >> ((3-(i & 3)) * 8) ) & 255);
4072  }
4073  memset(context, '\0', sizeof(*context));
4074  memset(&finalcount, '\0', sizeof(finalcount));
4075 }
4076 // END OF SHA1 CODE

4078 static void base64_encode(const unsigned char *src, int src_len, char *dst) {
4079  static const char *b64 =
4080  "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
4081  int i, j, a, b, c;
4082 
4083  for (i = j = 0; i < src_len; i += 3) {
4084  a = src[i];
4085  b = i + 1 >= src_len ? 0 : src[i + 1];
4086  c = i + 2 >= src_len ? 0 : src[i + 2];
4087 
4088  dst[j++] = b64[a >> 2];
4089  dst[j++] = b64[((a & 3) << 4) | (b >> 4)];
4090  if (i + 1 < src_len) {
4091  dst[j++] = b64[(b & 15) << 2 | (c >> 6)];
4092  }
4093  if (i + 2 < src_len) {
4094  dst[j++] = b64[c & 63];
4095  }
4096  }
4097  while (j % 4 != 0) {
4098  dst[j++] = '=';
4099  }
4100  dst[j++] = '\0';
4101 }

4103 static void send_websocket_handshake(struct mg_connection *conn) {
4104  static const char *magic = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11";
4105  char buf[100], sha[20], b64_sha[sizeof(sha) * 2];
4106  SHA1_CTX sha_ctx;
4107 
4108  mg_snprintf(conn, buf, sizeof(buf), "%s%s",
4109  mg_get_header(conn, "Sec-WebSocket-Key"), magic);
4110  SHA1Init(&sha_ctx);
4111  SHA1Update(&sha_ctx, (unsigned char *) buf, strlen(buf));
4112  SHA1Final((unsigned char *) sha, &sha_ctx);
4113  base64_encode((unsigned char *) sha, sizeof(sha), b64_sha);
4114  mg_printf(conn, "%s%s%s",
4115  "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n"
4116  "Upgrade: websocket\r\n"
4117  "Connection: Upgrade\r\n"
4118  "Sec-WebSocket-Accept: ", b64_sha, "\r\n\r\n");
4119 }

4121 static void read_websocket(struct mg_connection *conn) {
4122  // Pointer to the beginning of the portion of the incoming websocket message
4123  // queue. The original websocket upgrade request is never removed,
4124  // so the queue begins after it.
4125  unsigned char *buf = (unsigned char *) conn->buf + conn->request_len;
4126  int bits, n, stop = 0;
4127  size_t i, len, mask_len, data_len, header_len, body_len;
4128  // data points to the place where the message is stored when passed to the
4129  // websocket_data callback. This is either mem on the stack,
4130  // or a dynamically allocated buffer if it is too large.
4131  char mem[4 * 1024], mask[4], *data;
4132 
4133  assert(conn->content_len == 0);
4134 
4135  // Loop continuously, reading messages from the socket, invoking the callback,
4136  // and waiting repeatedly until an error occurs.
4137  while (!stop) {
4138  header_len = 0;
4139  // body_len is the length of the entire queue in bytes
4140  // len is the length of the current message
4141  // data_len is the length of the current message's data payload
4142  // header_len is the length of the current message's header
4143  if ((body_len = conn->data_len - conn->request_len) >= 2) {
4144  len = buf[1] & 127;
4145  mask_len = buf[1] & 128 ? 4 : 0;
4146  if (len < 126 && body_len >= mask_len) {
4147  data_len = len;
4148  header_len = 2 + mask_len;
4149  } else if (len == 126 && body_len >= 4 + mask_len) {
4150  header_len = 4 + mask_len;
4151  data_len = ((((int) buf[2]) << 8) + buf[3]);
4152  } else if (body_len >= 10 + mask_len) {
4153  header_len = 10 + mask_len;
4154  data_len = (((uint64_t) htonl(* (uint32_t *) &buf[2])) << 32) +
4155  htonl(* (uint32_t *) &buf[6]);
4156  }
4157  }
4158 
4159  // Data layout is as follows:
4160  // conn->buf buf
4161  // v v frame1 | frame2
4162  // |---------------------|----------------|--------------|-------
4163  // | |<--header_len-->|<--data_len-->|
4164  // |<-conn->request_len->|<-----body_len----------->|
4165  // |<-------------------conn->data_len------------->|
4166 
4167  if (header_len > 0) {
4168  // Allocate space to hold websocket payload
4169  data = mem;
4170  if (data_len > sizeof(mem) && (data = malloc(data_len)) == NULL) {
4171  // Allocation failed, exit the loop and then close the connection
4172  // TODO: notify user about the failure
4173  break;
4174  }
4175 
4176  // Save mask and bits, otherwise it may be clobbered by memmove below
4177  bits = buf[0];
4178  memcpy(mask, buf + header_len - mask_len, mask_len);
4179 
4180  // Read frame payload into the allocated buffer.
4181  assert(body_len >= header_len);
4182  if (data_len + header_len > body_len) {
4183  len = body_len - header_len;
4184  memcpy(data, buf + header_len, len);
4185  // TODO: handle pull error
4186  pull_all(NULL, conn, data + len, data_len - len);
4187  conn->data_len = conn->request_len;
4188  } else {
4189  len = data_len + header_len;
4190  memcpy(data, buf + header_len, data_len);
4191  memmove(buf, buf + len, body_len - len);
4192  conn->data_len -= len;
4193  }
4194 
4195  // Apply mask if necessary
4196  if (mask_len > 0) {
4197  for (i = 0; i < data_len; i++) {
4198  data[i] ^= mask[i % 4];
4199  }
4200  }
4201 
4202  // Exit the loop if callback signalled to exit,
4203  // or "connection close" opcode received.
4204  if ((bits & WEBSOCKET_OPCODE_CONNECTION_CLOSE) ||
4205  (conn->ctx->callbacks.websocket_data != NULL &&
4206  !conn->ctx->callbacks.websocket_data(conn, bits, data, data_len))) {
4207  stop = 1;
4208  }
4209 
4210  if (data != mem) {
4211  free(data);
4212  }
4213  // Not breaking the loop, process next websocket frame.
4214  } else {
4215  // Buffering websocket request
4216  if ((n = pull(NULL, conn, conn->buf + conn->data_len,
4217  conn->buf_size - conn->data_len)) <= 0) {
4218  break;
4219  }
4220  conn->data_len += n;
4221  }
4222  }
4223 }
4224 
4225 int mg_websocket_write(struct mg_connection* conn, int opcode,
4226  const char *data, size_t data_len) {
4227  unsigned char *copy;
4228  size_t copy_len = 0;
4229  int retval = -1;
4230 
4231  if ((copy = (unsigned char *) malloc(data_len + 10)) == NULL) {
4232  return -1;
4233  }
4234 
4235  copy[0] = 0x80 + (opcode & 0x0f);
4236 
4237  // Frame format: http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6455#section-5.2
4238  if (data_len < 126) {
4239  // Inline 7-bit length field
4240  copy[1] = data_len;
4241  memcpy(copy + 2, data, data_len);
4242  copy_len = 2 + data_len;
4243  } else if (data_len <= 0xFFFF) {
4244  // 16-bit length field
4245  copy[1] = 126;
4246  * (uint16_t *) (copy + 2) = htons(data_len);
4247  memcpy(copy + 4, data, data_len);
4248  copy_len = 4 + data_len;
4249  } else {
4250  // 64-bit length field
4251  copy[1] = 127;
4252  * (uint32_t *) (copy + 2) = htonl((uint64_t) data_len >> 32);
4253  * (uint32_t *) (copy + 6) = htonl(data_len & 0xffffffff);
4254  memcpy(copy + 10, data, data_len);
4255  copy_len = 10 + data_len;
4256  }
4257 
4258  // Not thread safe
4259  if (copy_len > 0) {
4260  retval = mg_write(conn, copy, copy_len);
4261  }
4262  free(copy);
4263 
4264  return retval;
4265 }

4267 static void handle_websocket_request(struct mg_connection *conn) {
4268  const char *version = mg_get_header(conn, "Sec-WebSocket-Version");
4269  if (version == NULL || strcmp(version, "13") != 0) {
4270  send_http_error(conn, 426, "Upgrade Required", "%s", "Upgrade Required");
4271  } else if (conn->ctx->callbacks.websocket_connect != NULL &&
4272  conn->ctx->callbacks.websocket_connect(conn) != 0) {
4273  // Callback has returned non-zero, do not proceed with handshake
4274  } else {
4275  send_websocket_handshake(conn);
4276  if (conn->ctx->callbacks.websocket_ready != NULL) {
4277  conn->ctx->callbacks.websocket_ready(conn);
4278  }
4279  read_websocket(conn);
4280  }
4281 }

4283 static int is_websocket_request(const struct mg_connection *conn) {

4299 static int isbyte(int n) {
4300  return n >= 0 && n <= 255;
4301 }
4302 
4303 static int parse_net(const char *spec, uint32_t *net, uint32_t *mask) {
4304  int n, a, b, c, d, slash = 32, len = 0;
4305 
4306  if ((sscanf(spec, "%d.%d.%d.%d/%d%n", &a, &b, &c, &d, &slash, &n) == 5 ||
4307  sscanf(spec, "%d.%d.%d.%d%n", &a, &b, &c, &d, &n) == 4) &&
4308  isbyte(a) && isbyte(b) && isbyte(c) && isbyte(d) &&
4309  slash >= 0 && slash < 33) {
4310  len = n;
4311  *net = ((uint32_t)a << 24) | ((uint32_t)b << 16) | ((uint32_t)c << 8) | d;
4312  *mask = slash ? 0xffffffffU << (32 - slash) : 0;
4313  }
4314 
4315  return len;
4316 }

4318 static int set_throttle(const char *spec, uint32_t remote_ip, const char *uri) {
4319  int throttle = 0;
4320  struct vec vec, val;
4321  uint32_t net, mask;
4322  char mult;
4323  double v;
4324 
4325  while ((spec = next_option(spec, &vec, &val)) != NULL) {
4326  mult = ',';
4327  if (sscanf(val.ptr, "%lf%c", &v, &mult) < 1 || v < 0 ||
4328  (lowercase(&mult) != 'k' && lowercase(&mult) != 'm' && mult != ',')) {
4329  continue;
4330  }
4331  v *= lowercase(&mult) == 'k' ? 1024 : lowercase(&mult) == 'm' ? 1048576 : 1;
4332  if (vec.len == 1 && vec.ptr[0] == '*') {
4333  throttle = (int) v;
4334  } else if (parse_net(vec.ptr, &net, &mask) > 0) {
4335  if ((remote_ip & mask) == net) {
4336  throttle = (int) v;
4337  }
4338  } else if (match_prefix(vec.ptr, vec.len, uri) > 0) {
4339  throttle = (int) v;
4340  }
4341  }
4342 
4343  return throttle;
4344 }

4354 int mg_upload(struct mg_connection *conn, const char *destination_dir) {
4355  const char *content_type_header, *boundary_start;
4356  char buf[MG_BUF_LEN], path[PATH_MAX], fname[1024], boundary[100], *s;
4357  FILE *fp;
4358  int bl, n, i, j, headers_len, boundary_len, eof,
4359  len = 0, num_uploaded_files = 0;
4360 
4361  // Request looks like this:
4362  //
4363  // POST /upload HTTP/1.1
4364  // Host: 127.0.0.1:8080
4365  // Content-Length: 244894
4366  // Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundaryRVr
4367  //
4368  // ------WebKitFormBoundaryRVr
4369  // Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="accum.png"
4370  // Content-Type: image/png
4371  //
4372  // <89>PNG
4373  // <PNG DATA>
4374  // ------WebKitFormBoundaryRVr
4375 
4376  // Extract boundary string from the Content-Type header
4377  if ((content_type_header = mg_get_header(conn, "Content-Type")) == NULL ||
4378  (boundary_start = mg_strcasestr(content_type_header,
4379  "boundary=")) == NULL ||
4380  (sscanf(boundary_start, "boundary=\"%99[^\"]\"", boundary) == 0 &&
4381  sscanf(boundary_start, "boundary=%99s", boundary) == 0) ||
4382  boundary[0] == '\0') {
4383  return num_uploaded_files;
4384  }
4385 
4386  boundary_len = strlen(boundary);
4387  bl = boundary_len + 4; // \r\n--<boundary>
4388  for (;;) {
4389  // Pull in headers
4390  assert(len >= 0 && len <= (int) sizeof(buf));
4391  while ((n = mg_read(conn, buf + len, sizeof(buf) - len)) > 0) {
4392  len += n;
4393  }
4394  if ((headers_len = get_request_len(buf, len)) <= 0) {
4395  break;
4396  }
4397 
4398  // Fetch file name.
4399  fname[0] = '\0';
4400  for (i = j = 0; i < headers_len; i++) {
4401  if (buf[i] == '\r' && buf[i + 1] == '\n') {
4402  buf[i] = buf[i + 1] = '\0';
4403  // TODO(lsm): don't expect filename to be the 3rd field,
4404  // parse the header properly instead.
4405  sscanf(&buf[j], "Content-Disposition: %*s %*s filename=\"%1023[^\"]",
4406  fname);
4407  j = i + 2;
4408  }
4409  }
4410 
4411  // Give up if the headers are not what we expect
4412  if (fname[0] == '\0') {
4413  break;
4414  }
4415 
4416  // Move data to the beginning of the buffer
4417  assert(len >= headers_len);
4418  memmove(buf, &buf[headers_len], len - headers_len);
4419  len -= headers_len;
4420 
4421  // We open the file with exclusive lock held. This guarantee us
4422  // there is no other thread can save into the same file simultaneously.
4423  fp = NULL;
4424  // Construct destination file name. Do not allow paths to have slashes.
4425  if ((s = strrchr(fname, '/')) == NULL &&
4426  (s = strrchr(fname, '\\')) == NULL) {
4427  s = fname;
4428  }
4429 
4430  // Open file in binary mode. TODO: set an exclusive lock.
4431  snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s/%s", destination_dir, s);
4432  if ((fp = fopen(path, "wb")) == NULL) {
4433  break;
4434  }
4435 
4436  // Read POST data, write into file until boundary is found.
4437  eof = n = 0;
4438  do {
4439  len += n;
4440  for (i = 0; i < len - bl; i++) {
4441  if (!memcmp(&buf[i], "\r\n--", 4) &&
4442  !memcmp(&buf[i + 4], boundary, boundary_len)) {
4443  // Found boundary, that's the end of file data.
4444  fwrite(buf, 1, i, fp);
4445  eof = 1;
4446  memmove(buf, &buf[i + bl], len - (i + bl));
4447  len -= i + bl;
4448  break;
4449  }
4450  }
4451  if (!eof && len > bl) {
4452  fwrite(buf, 1, len - bl, fp);
4453  memmove(buf, &buf[len - bl], bl);
4454  len = bl;
4455  }
4456  } while (!eof && (n = mg_read(conn, buf + len, sizeof(buf) - len)) > 0);
4457  fclose(fp);
4458  if (eof) {
4459  num_uploaded_files++;
4460  if (conn->ctx->callbacks.upload != NULL) {
4461  conn->ctx->callbacks.upload(conn, path);
4462  }
4463  }
4464  }
4465 
4466  return num_uploaded_files;
4467 }

4489  sscanf(host_header, "%1024[^:]", host) == 0) {

4499 // This is the heart of the Mongoose's logic.
4500 // This function is called when the request is read, parsed and validated,
4501 // and Mongoose must decide what action to take: serve a file, or
4502 // a directory, or call embedded function, etcetera.
4503 static void handle_request(struct mg_connection *conn) {
4504  struct mg_request_info *ri = &conn->request_info;
4505  char path[PATH_MAX];
4506  int uri_len, ssl_index;
4507  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
4508 
4509  if ((conn->request_info.query_string = strchr(ri->uri, '?')) != NULL) {
4510  * ((char *) conn->request_info.query_string++) = '\0';
4511  }
4512  uri_len = (int) strlen(ri->uri);
4513  mg_url_decode(ri->uri, uri_len, (char *) ri->uri, uri_len + 1, 0);
4514  remove_double_dots_and_double_slashes((char *) ri->uri);
4515  convert_uri_to_file_name(conn, path, sizeof(path), &file);
4516  conn->throttle = set_throttle(conn->ctx->config[THROTTLE],
4517  get_remote_ip(conn), ri->uri);
4518 
4519  DEBUG_TRACE(("%s", ri->uri));
4520  // Perform redirect and auth checks before calling begin_request() handler.
4521  // Otherwise, begin_request() would need to perform auth checks and redirects.
4522  if (!conn->client.is_ssl && conn->client.ssl_redir &&
4523  (ssl_index = get_first_ssl_listener_index(conn->ctx)) > -1) {
4524  redirect_to_https_port(conn, ssl_index);
4525  } else if (!is_put_or_delete_request(conn) &&
4526  !check_authorization(conn, path)) {
4527  send_authorization_request(conn);
4528  } else if (conn->ctx->callbacks.begin_request != NULL &&
4529  conn->ctx->callbacks.begin_request(conn)) {
4530  // Do nothing, callback has served the request
4531 #if defined(USE_WEBSOCKET)
4532  } else if (is_websocket_request(conn)) {
4533  handle_websocket_request(conn);
4534 #endif
4535  } else if (!strcmp(ri->request_method, "OPTIONS")) {
4536  send_options(conn);
4537  } else if (conn->ctx->config[DOCUMENT_ROOT] == NULL) {
4538  send_http_error(conn, 404, "Not Found", "Not Found");
4539  } else if (is_put_or_delete_request(conn) &&
4540  (is_authorized_for_put(conn) != 1)) {
4541  send_authorization_request(conn);
4542  } else if (!strcmp(ri->request_method, "PUT")) {
4543  put_file(conn, path);
4544  } else if (!strcmp(ri->request_method, "MKCOL")) {
4545  mkcol(conn, path);
4546  } else if (!strcmp(ri->request_method, "DELETE")) {
4547  struct de de;
4548  memset(&de.file, 0, sizeof(de.file));
4549  if(!mg_stat(conn, path, &de.file)) {
4550  send_http_error(conn, 404, "Not Found", "%s", "File not found");
4551  } else {
4552  if(de.file.modification_time) {
4553  if(de.file.is_directory) {
4554  remove_directory(conn, path);
4555  send_http_error(conn, 204, "No Content", "%s", "");
4556  } else if (mg_remove(path) == 0) {
4557  send_http_error(conn, 204, "No Content", "%s", "");
4558  } else {
4559  send_http_error(conn, 423, "Locked", "remove(%s): %s", path,
4560  strerror(ERRNO));
4561  }
4562  }
4563  else {
4564  send_http_error(conn, 500, http_500_error, "remove(%s): %s", path,
4565  strerror(ERRNO));
4566  }
4567  }
4568  } else if ((file.membuf == NULL && file.modification_time == (time_t) 0) ||
4569  must_hide_file(conn, path)) {
4570  send_http_error(conn, 404, "Not Found", "%s", "File not found");
4571  } else if (file.is_directory && ri->uri[uri_len - 1] != '/') {
4572  mg_printf(conn, "HTTP/1.1 301 Moved Permanently\r\n"
4573  "Location: %s/\r\n\r\n", ri->uri);
4574  } else if (!strcmp(ri->request_method, "PROPFIND")) {
4575  handle_propfind(conn, path, &file);
4576  } else if (file.is_directory &&
4577  !substitute_index_file(conn, path, sizeof(path), &file)) {
4578  if (!mg_strcasecmp(conn->ctx->config[ENABLE_DIRECTORY_LISTING], "yes")) {
4579  handle_directory_request(conn, path);
4580  } else {
4581  send_http_error(conn, 403, "Directory Listing Denied",
4582  "Directory listing denied");
4583  }
4584 #ifdef USE_LUA
4585  } else if (match_prefix("**.lp$", 6, path) > 0) {
4586  handle_lsp_request(conn, path, &file, NULL);
4587 #endif
4588 #if !defined(NO_CGI)
4589  } else if (match_prefix(conn->ctx->config[CGI_EXTENSIONS],
4590  strlen(conn->ctx->config[CGI_EXTENSIONS]),
4591  path) > 0) {
4592  if (strcmp(ri->request_method, "POST") &&
4593  strcmp(ri->request_method, "HEAD") &&
4594  strcmp(ri->request_method, "GET")) {
4595  send_http_error(conn, 501, "Not Implemented",
4596  "Method %s is not implemented", ri->request_method);
4597  } else {
4598  handle_cgi_request(conn, path);
4599  }
4600 #endif // !NO_CGI
4601  } else if (match_prefix(conn->ctx->config[SSI_EXTENSIONS],
4602  strlen(conn->ctx->config[SSI_EXTENSIONS]),
4603  path) > 0) {
4604  handle_ssi_file_request(conn, path);
4605  } else if (is_not_modified(conn, path, &file)) {
4606  send_http_error(conn, 304, "Not Modified", "%s", "");
4607  } else {
4608  handle_file_request(conn, path, &file);
4609  }
4610 }

4620 static int is_valid_port(unsigned int port) {
4621  return port > 0 && port < 0xffff;
4622 }
4623 
4624 // Valid listening port specification is: [ip_address:]port[s]
4625 // Examples: 80, 443s, 127.0.0.1:3128, 1.2.3.4:8080s
4626 // TODO(lsm): add parsing of the IPv6 address
4627 static int parse_port_string(const struct vec *vec, struct socket *so) {
4628  unsigned int a, b, c, d, ch, len, port;
4629 #if defined(USE_IPV6)
4630  char buf[100];
4631 #endif
4632 
4633  // MacOS needs that. If we do not zero it, subsequent bind() will fail.
4634  // Also, all-zeroes in the socket address means binding to all addresses
4635  // for both IPv4 and IPv6 (INADDR_ANY and IN6ADDR_ANY_INIT).
4636  memset(so, 0, sizeof(*so));
4637  so->lsa.sin.sin_family = AF_INET;
4638 
4639  if (sscanf(vec->ptr, "%u.%u.%u.%u:%u%n", &a, &b, &c, &d, &port, &len) == 5) {
4640  // Bind to a specific IPv4 address, e.g. 192.168.1.5:8080
4641  so->lsa.sin.sin_addr.s_addr = htonl((a << 24) | (b << 16) | (c << 8) | d);
4642  so->lsa.sin.sin_port = htons((uint16_t) port);
4643 #if defined(USE_IPV6)
4644 
4645  } else if (sscanf(vec->ptr, "[%49[^]]]:%d%n", buf, &port, &len) == 2 &&
4646  inet_pton(AF_INET6, buf, &so->lsa.sin6.sin6_addr)) {
4647  // IPv6 address, e.g. [3ffe:2a00:100:7031::1]:8080
4648  so->lsa.sin6.sin6_family = AF_INET6;
4649  so->lsa.sin6.sin6_port = htons((uint16_t) port);
4650 #endif
4651  } else if (sscanf(vec->ptr, "%u%n", &port, &len) == 1) {
4652  // If only port is specified, bind to IPv4, INADDR_ANY
4653  so->lsa.sin.sin_port = htons((uint16_t) port);
4654  } else {
4655  port = len = 0; // Parsing failure. Make port invalid.
4656  }
4657 
4658  ch = vec->ptr[len]; // Next character after the port number
4659  so->is_ssl = ch == 's';
4660  so->ssl_redir = ch == 'r';
4661 
4662  // Make sure the port is valid and vector ends with 's', 'r' or ','
4663  return is_valid_port(port) &&
4664  (ch == '\0' || ch == 's' || ch == 'r' || ch == ',');
4665 }

4667 static int set_ports_option(struct mg_context *ctx) {
4668  const char *list = ctx->config[LISTENING_PORTS];
4669  int on = 1, success = 1;
4670 #if defined(USE_IPV6)
4671  int off = 0;
4672 #endif
4673  struct vec vec;
4674  struct socket so, *ptr;
4675 
4676  while (success && (list = next_option(list, &vec, NULL)) != NULL) {
4677  if (!parse_port_string(&vec, &so)) {
4678  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: %.*s: invalid port spec. Expecting list of: %s",
4679  __func__, (int) vec.len, vec.ptr, "[IP_ADDRESS:]PORT[s|r]");
4680  success = 0;
4681  } else if (so.is_ssl && ctx->ssl_ctx == NULL) {
4682  cry(fc(ctx), "Cannot add SSL socket, is -ssl_certificate option set?");
4683  success = 0;
4684  } else if ((so.sock = socket(so.lsa.sa.sa_family, SOCK_STREAM, 6)) ==
4685  INVALID_SOCKET ||
4686  // On Windows, SO_REUSEADDR is recommended only for
4687  // broadcast UDP sockets
4688  setsockopt(so.sock, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR,
4689  (void *) &on, sizeof(on)) != 0 ||
4690 #if defined(USE_IPV6)
4691  (so.lsa.sa.sa_family == AF_INET6 &&
4692  setsockopt(so.sock, IPPROTO_IPV6, IPV6_V6ONLY, (void *) &off,
4693  sizeof(off)) != 0) ||
4694 #endif
4695  bind(so.sock, &so.lsa.sa, so.lsa.sa.sa_family == AF_INET ?
4696  sizeof(so.lsa.sin) : sizeof(so.lsa)) != 0 ||
4697  listen(so.sock, SOMAXCONN) != 0) {
4698  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: cannot bind to %.*s: %d (%s)", __func__,
4699  (int) vec.len, vec.ptr, ERRNO, strerror(errno));
4700  closesocket(so.sock);
4701  success = 0;
4702  } else if ((ptr = (struct socket *) realloc(ctx->listening_sockets,
4703  (ctx->num_listening_sockets + 1) *
4704  sizeof(ctx->listening_sockets[0]))) == NULL) {
4705  closesocket(so.sock);
4706  success = 0;
4707  } else {
4708  set_close_on_exec(so.sock);
4709  ctx->listening_sockets = ptr;
4710  ctx->listening_sockets[ctx->num_listening_sockets] = so;
4711  ctx->num_listening_sockets++;
4712  }
4713  }
4714 
4715  if (!success) {
4716  close_all_listening_sockets(ctx);
4717  }
4718 
4719  return success;
4720 }

4765 // Verify given socket address against the ACL.
4766 // Return -1 if ACL is malformed, 0 if address is disallowed, 1 if allowed.
4767 static int check_acl(struct mg_context *ctx, uint32_t remote_ip) {
4768  int allowed, flag;
4769  uint32_t net, mask;
4770  struct vec vec;
4771  const char *list = ctx->config[ACCESS_CONTROL_LIST];
4772 
4773  // If any ACL is set, deny by default
4774  allowed = list == NULL ? '+' : '-';
4775 
4776  while ((list = next_option(list, &vec, NULL)) != NULL) {
4777  flag = vec.ptr[0];
4778  if ((flag != '+' && flag != '-') ||
4779  parse_net(&vec.ptr[1], &net, &mask) == 0) {
4780  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: subnet must be [+|-]x.x.x.x[/x]", __func__);
4781  return -1;
4782  }
4783 
4784  if (net == (remote_ip & mask)) {
4785  allowed = flag;
4786  }
4787  }
4788 
4789  return allowed == '+';
4790 }

4832 static void ssl_locking_callback(int mode, int mutex_num, const char *file,
4833  int line) {

4835  (void) file;

4848 #if !defined(NO_SSL_DL)
4849 static int load_dll(struct mg_context *ctx, const char *dll_name,
4850  struct ssl_func *sw) {
4851  union {void *p; void (*fp)(void);} u;
4852  void *dll_handle;
4853  struct ssl_func *fp;
4854 
4855  if ((dll_handle = dlopen(dll_name, RTLD_LAZY)) == NULL) {
4856  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: cannot load %s", __func__, dll_name);
4857  return 0;
4858  }
4859 
4860  for (fp = sw; fp->name != NULL; fp++) {
4861 #ifdef _WIN32
4862  // GetProcAddress() returns pointer to function
4863  u.fp = (void (*)(void)) dlsym(dll_handle, fp->name);
4864 #else
4865  // dlsym() on UNIX returns void *. ISO C forbids casts of data pointers to
4866  // function pointers. We need to use a union to make a cast.
4867  u.p = dlsym(dll_handle, fp->name);
4868 #endif // _WIN32
4869  if (u.fp == NULL) {
4870  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: %s: cannot find %s", __func__, dll_name, fp->name);
4871  return 0;
4872  } else {
4873  fp->ptr = u.fp;
4874  }
4875  }
4876 
4877  return 1;
4878 }
4879 #endif // NO_SSL_DL

4881 // Dynamically load SSL library. Set up ctx->ssl_ctx pointer.
4882 static int set_ssl_option(struct mg_context *ctx) {
4883  int i, size;
4884  const char *pem;
4885 
4886  // If PEM file is not specified and the init_ssl callback
4887  // is not specified, skip SSL initialization.
4888  if ((pem = ctx->config[SSL_CERTIFICATE]) == NULL &&
4889  ctx->callbacks.init_ssl == NULL) {
4890  return 1;
4891  }
4892 
4893 #if !defined(NO_SSL_DL)
4894  if (!load_dll(ctx, SSL_LIB, ssl_sw) ||
4895  !load_dll(ctx, CRYPTO_LIB, crypto_sw)) {
4896  return 0;
4897  }
4898 #endif // NO_SSL_DL
4899 
4900  // Initialize SSL library
4901  SSL_library_init();
4902  SSL_load_error_strings();
4903 
4904  if ((ctx->ssl_ctx = SSL_CTX_new(SSLv23_server_method())) == NULL) {
4905  cry(fc(ctx), "SSL_CTX_new (server) error: %s", ssl_error());
4906  return 0;
4907  }
4908 
4909  // If user callback returned non-NULL, that means that user callback has
4910  // set up certificate itself. In this case, skip sertificate setting.
4911  if ((ctx->callbacks.init_ssl == NULL ||
4912  !ctx->callbacks.init_ssl(ctx->ssl_ctx, ctx->user_data)) &&
4913  (SSL_CTX_use_certificate_file(ctx->ssl_ctx, pem, 1) == 0 ||
4914  SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey_file(ctx->ssl_ctx, pem, 1) == 0)) {
4915  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: cannot open %s: %s", __func__, pem, ssl_error());
4916  return 0;
4917  }
4918 
4919  if (pem != NULL) {
4920  (void) SSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain_file(ctx->ssl_ctx, pem);
4921  }
4922 
4923  // Initialize locking callbacks, needed for thread safety.
4924  // http://www.openssl.org/support/faq.html#PROG1
4925  size = sizeof(pthread_mutex_t) * CRYPTO_num_locks();
4926  if ((ssl_mutexes = (pthread_mutex_t *) malloc((size_t)size)) == NULL) {
4927  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: cannot allocate mutexes: %s", __func__, ssl_error());
4928  return 0;
4929  }
4930 
4931  for (i = 0; i < CRYPTO_num_locks(); i++) {
4932  pthread_mutex_init(&ssl_mutexes[i], NULL);
4933  }
4934 
4935  CRYPTO_set_locking_callback(&ssl_locking_callback);
4936  CRYPTO_set_id_callback(&ssl_id_callback);
4937 
4938  return 1;
4939 }
4940 
4941 static void uninitialize_ssl(struct mg_context *ctx) {
4942  int i;
4943  if (ctx->ssl_ctx != NULL) {
4944  CRYPTO_set_locking_callback(NULL);
4945  for (i = 0; i < CRYPTO_num_locks(); i++) {
4946  pthread_mutex_destroy(&ssl_mutexes[i]);
4947  }
4948  CRYPTO_set_locking_callback(NULL);
4949  CRYPTO_set_id_callback(NULL);
4950  }
4951 }

4954 static int set_gpass_option(struct mg_context *ctx) {
4955  struct file file = STRUCT_FILE_INITIALIZER;
4956  const char *path = ctx->config[GLOBAL_PASSWORDS_FILE];
4957  if (path != NULL && !mg_stat(fc(ctx), path, &file)) {
4958  cry(fc(ctx), "Cannot open %s: %s", path, strerror(ERRNO));
4959  return 0;
4960  }
4961  return 1;
4962 }

4964 static int set_acl_option(struct mg_context *ctx) {
4965  return check_acl(ctx, (uint32_t) 0x7f000001UL) != -1;
4966 }

4968 static void reset_per_request_attributes(struct mg_connection *conn) {
4969  conn->path_info = NULL;
4970  conn->num_bytes_sent = conn->consumed_content = 0;
4971  conn->status_code = -1;
4972  conn->must_close = conn->request_len = conn->throttle = 0;
4973 }
4974 
4975 static void close_socket_gracefully(struct mg_connection *conn) {
4976 #if defined(_WIN32)
4977  char buf[MG_BUF_LEN];
4978  int n;
4979 #endif
4980  struct linger linger;
4981 
4982  // Set linger option to avoid socket hanging out after close. This prevent
4983  // ephemeral port exhaust problem under high QPS.
4984  linger.l_onoff = 1;
4985  linger.l_linger = 1;
4986  setsockopt(conn->client.sock, SOL_SOCKET, SO_LINGER,
4987  (char *) &linger, sizeof(linger));
4988 
4989  // Send FIN to the client
4990  shutdown(conn->client.sock, SHUT_WR);
4991  set_non_blocking_mode(conn->client.sock);
4992 
4993 #if defined(_WIN32)
4994  // Read and discard pending incoming data. If we do not do that and close the
4995  // socket, the data in the send buffer may be discarded. This
4996  // behaviour is seen on Windows, when client keeps sending data
4997  // when server decides to close the connection; then when client
4998  // does recv() it gets no data back.
4999  do {
5000  n = pull(NULL, conn, buf, sizeof(buf));
5001  } while (n > 0);
5002 #endif
5003 
5004  // Now we know that our FIN is ACK-ed, safe to close
5005  closesocket(conn->client.sock);
5006 }
5007 
5008 static void close_connection(struct mg_connection *conn) {
5009  conn->must_close = 1;
5010 
5011 #ifndef NO_SSL
5012  if (conn->ssl != NULL) {
5013  // Run SSL_shutdown twice to ensure completly close SSL connection
5014  SSL_shutdown(conn->ssl);
5015  SSL_free(conn->ssl);
5016  conn->ssl = NULL;
5017  }
5018 #endif
5019  if (conn->client.sock != INVALID_SOCKET) {
5020  close_socket_gracefully(conn);
5021  conn->client.sock = INVALID_SOCKET;
5022  }
5023 }

5025 void mg_close_connection(struct mg_connection *conn) {
5026 #ifndef NO_SSL
5027  if (conn->client_ssl_ctx != NULL) {
5028  SSL_CTX_free((SSL_CTX *) conn->client_ssl_ctx);
5029  }
5030 #endif
5031  close_connection(conn);
5032  free(conn);
5033 }

5035 static struct mg_connection *mg_connect(const char *host, int port, int use_ssl,
5036  char *ebuf, size_t ebuf_len) {
5037  static struct mg_context fake_ctx;
5038  struct mg_connection *conn = NULL;
5039  SOCKET sock;
5040 
5041  if ((sock = conn2(host, port, use_ssl, ebuf, ebuf_len)) == INVALID_SOCKET) {
5042  } else if ((conn = (struct mg_connection *)
5043  calloc(1, sizeof(*conn) + MAX_REQUEST_SIZE)) == NULL) {
5044  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "calloc(): %s", strerror(ERRNO));
5045  closesocket(sock);
5046 #ifndef NO_SSL
5047  } else if (use_ssl && (conn->client_ssl_ctx =
5048  SSL_CTX_new(SSLv23_client_method())) == NULL) {
5049  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "SSL_CTX_new error");
5050  closesocket(sock);
5051  free(conn);
5052  conn = NULL;
5053 #endif // NO_SSL
5054  } else {
5055  socklen_t len = sizeof(struct sockaddr);
5056  conn->buf_size = MAX_REQUEST_SIZE;
5057  conn->buf = (char *) (conn + 1);
5058  conn->ctx = &fake_ctx;
5059  conn->client.sock = sock;
5060  getsockname(sock, &conn->client.rsa.sa, &len);
5061  conn->client.is_ssl = use_ssl;
5062 #ifndef NO_SSL
5063  if (use_ssl) {
5064  // SSL_CTX_set_verify call is needed to switch off server certificate
5065  // checking, which is off by default in OpenSSL and on in yaSSL.
5066  SSL_CTX_set_verify(conn->client_ssl_ctx, 0, 0);
5067  sslize(conn, conn->client_ssl_ctx, SSL_connect);
5068  }
5069 #endif
5070  }
5071 
5072  return conn;
5073 }

5075 static int is_valid_uri(const char *uri) {
5076  // Conform to http://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec5.html#sec5.1.2
5077  // URI can be an asterisk (*) or should start with slash.
5078  return uri[0] == '/' || (uri[0] == '*' && uri[1] == '\0');
5079 }

5081 static int getreq(struct mg_connection *conn, char *ebuf, size_t ebuf_len) {
5082  const char *cl;
5083 
5084  ebuf[0] = '\0';
5085  reset_per_request_attributes(conn);
5086  conn->request_len = read_request(NULL, conn, conn->buf, conn->buf_size,
5087  &conn->data_len);
5088  assert(conn->request_len < 0 || conn->data_len >= conn->request_len);
5089 
5090  if (conn->request_len == 0 && conn->data_len == conn->buf_size) {
5091  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "%s", "Request Too Large");
5092  } else if (conn->request_len <= 0) {
5093  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "%s", "Client closed connection");
5094  } else if (parse_http_message(conn->buf, conn->buf_size,
5095  &conn->request_info) <= 0) {
5096  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "Bad request: [%.*s]", conn->data_len, conn->buf);
5097  } else {
5098  // Request is valid
5099  if ((cl = get_header(&conn->request_info, "Content-Length")) != NULL) {
5100  conn->content_len = strtoll(cl, NULL, 10);
5101  } else if (!mg_strcasecmp(conn->request_info.request_method, "POST") ||
5102  !mg_strcasecmp(conn->request_info.request_method, "PUT")) {
5103  conn->content_len = -1;
5104  } else {
5105  conn->content_len = 0;
5106  }
5107  conn->birth_time = time(NULL);
5108  }
5109  return ebuf[0] == '\0';
5110 }
5111 
5112 struct mg_connection *mg_download(const char *host, int port, int use_ssl,
5113  char *ebuf, size_t ebuf_len,
5114  const char *fmt, ...) {
5115  struct mg_connection *conn;
5116  va_list ap;
5117 
5118  va_start(ap, fmt);
5119  ebuf[0] = '\0';
5120  if ((conn = mg_connect(host, port, use_ssl, ebuf, ebuf_len)) == NULL) {
5121  } else if (mg_vprintf(conn, fmt, ap) <= 0) {
5122  snprintf(ebuf, ebuf_len, "%s", "Error sending request");
5123  } else {
5124  getreq(conn, ebuf, ebuf_len);
5125  }
5126  if (ebuf[0] != '\0' && conn != NULL) {
5127  mg_close_connection(conn);
5128  conn = NULL;
5129  }
5130 
5131  return conn;
5132 }
5133 
5134 static void process_new_connection(struct mg_connection *conn) {
5135  struct mg_request_info *ri = &conn->request_info;
5136  int keep_alive_enabled, keep_alive, discard_len;
5137  char ebuf[100];
5138 
5139  keep_alive_enabled = !strcmp(conn->ctx->config[ENABLE_KEEP_ALIVE], "yes");
5140  keep_alive = 0;
5141 
5142  // Important: on new connection, reset the receiving buffer. Credit goes
5143  // to crule42.
5144  conn->data_len = 0;
5145  do {
5146  if (!getreq(conn, ebuf, sizeof(ebuf))) {
5147  send_http_error(conn, 500, "Server Error", "%s", ebuf);
5148  conn->must_close = 1;
5149  } else if (!is_valid_uri(conn->request_info.uri)) {
5150  snprintf(ebuf, sizeof(ebuf), "Invalid URI: [%s]", ri->uri);
5151  send_http_error(conn, 400, "Bad Request", "%s", ebuf);
5152  } else if (strcmp(ri->http_version, "1.0") &&
5153  strcmp(ri->http_version, "1.1")) {
5154  snprintf(ebuf, sizeof(ebuf), "Bad HTTP version: [%s]", ri->http_version);
5155  send_http_error(conn, 505, "Bad HTTP version", "%s", ebuf);
5156  }
5157 
5158  if (ebuf[0] == '\0') {
5159  handle_request(conn);
5160  if (conn->ctx->callbacks.end_request != NULL) {
5161  conn->ctx->callbacks.end_request(conn, conn->status_code);
5162  }
5163  log_access(conn);
5164  }
5165  if (ri->remote_user != NULL) {
5166  free((void *) ri->remote_user);
5167  // Important! When having connections with and without auth
5168  // would cause double free and then crash
5169  ri->remote_user = NULL;
5170  }
5171 
5172  // NOTE(lsm): order is important here. should_keep_alive() call
5173  // is using parsed request, which will be invalid after memmove's below.
5174  // Therefore, memorize should_keep_alive() result now for later use
5175  // in loop exit condition.
5176  keep_alive = conn->ctx->stop_flag == 0 && keep_alive_enabled &&
5177  conn->content_len >= 0 && should_keep_alive(conn);
5178 
5179  // Discard all buffered data for this request
5180  discard_len = conn->content_len >= 0 && conn->request_len > 0 &&
5181  conn->request_len + conn->content_len < (int64_t) conn->data_len ?
5182  (int) (conn->request_len + conn->content_len) : conn->data_len;
5183  assert(discard_len >= 0);
5184  memmove(conn->buf, conn->buf + discard_len, conn->data_len - discard_len);
5185  conn->data_len -= discard_len;
5186  assert(conn->data_len >= 0);
5187  assert(conn->data_len <= conn->buf_size);
5188  } while (keep_alive);
5189 }
5190 
5191 // Worker threads take accepted socket from the queue
5192 static int consume_socket(struct mg_context *ctx, struct socket *sp) {
5193  (void) pthread_mutex_lock(&ctx->mutex);
5194  DEBUG_TRACE(("going idle"));
5195 
5196  // If the queue is empty, wait. We're idle at this point.
5197  while (ctx->sq_head == ctx->sq_tail && ctx->stop_flag == 0) {
5198  pthread_cond_wait(&ctx->sq_full, &ctx->mutex);
5199  }
5200 
5201  // If we're stopping, sq_head may be equal to sq_tail.
5202  if (ctx->sq_head > ctx->sq_tail) {
5203  // Copy socket from the queue and increment tail
5204  *sp = ctx->queue[ctx->sq_tail % ARRAY_SIZE(ctx->queue)];
5205  ctx->sq_tail++;
5206  DEBUG_TRACE(("grabbed socket %d, going busy", sp->sock));
5207 
5208  // Wrap pointers if needed
5209  while (ctx->sq_tail > (int) ARRAY_SIZE(ctx->queue)) {
5210  ctx->sq_tail -= ARRAY_SIZE(ctx->queue);
5211  ctx->sq_head -= ARRAY_SIZE(ctx->queue);
5212  }
5213  }
5214 
5215  (void) pthread_cond_signal(&ctx->sq_empty);
5216  (void) pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->mutex);
5217 
5218  return !ctx->stop_flag;
5219 }
5220 
5221 static void *worker_thread(void *thread_func_param) {
5222  struct mg_context *ctx = (struct mg_context *) thread_func_param;
5223  struct mg_connection *conn;
5224 
5225  conn = (struct mg_connection *) calloc(1, sizeof(*conn) + MAX_REQUEST_SIZE);
5226  if (conn == NULL) {
5227  cry(fc(ctx), "%s", "Cannot create new connection struct, OOM");
5228  } else {
5229  conn->buf_size = MAX_REQUEST_SIZE;
5230  conn->buf = (char *) (conn + 1);
5231  conn->ctx = ctx;
5232  conn->request_info.user_data = ctx->user_data;
5233 
5234  // Call consume_socket() even when ctx->stop_flag > 0, to let it signal
5235  // sq_empty condvar to wake up the master waiting in produce_socket()
5236  while (consume_socket(ctx, &conn->client)) {
5237  conn->birth_time = time(NULL);
5238 
5239  // Fill in IP, port info early so even if SSL setup below fails,
5240  // error handler would have the corresponding info.
5241  // Thanks to Johannes Winkelmann for the patch.
5242  // TODO(lsm): Fix IPv6 case
5243  conn->request_info.remote_port = ntohs(conn->client.rsa.sin.sin_port);
5244  memcpy(&conn->request_info.remote_ip,
5245  &conn->client.rsa.sin.sin_addr.s_addr, 4);
5246  conn->request_info.remote_ip = ntohl(conn->request_info.remote_ip);
5247  conn->request_info.is_ssl = conn->client.is_ssl;
5248 
5249  if (!conn->client.is_ssl
5250 #ifndef NO_SSL
5251  || sslize(conn, conn->ctx->ssl_ctx, SSL_accept)
5252 #endif
5253  ) {
5254  process_new_connection(conn);
5255  }
5256 
5257  close_connection(conn);
5258  }
5259  free(conn);
5260  }
5261 
5262  // Signal master that we're done with connection and exiting
5263  (void) pthread_mutex_lock(&ctx->mutex);
5264  ctx->num_threads--;
5265  (void) pthread_cond_signal(&ctx->cond);
5266  assert(ctx->num_threads >= 0);
5267  (void) pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->mutex);
5268 
5269  DEBUG_TRACE(("exiting"));
5270  return NULL;
5271 }
5272 
5273 // Master thread adds accepted socket to a queue
5274 static void produce_socket(struct mg_context *ctx, const struct socket *sp) {
5275  (void) pthread_mutex_lock(&ctx->mutex);
5276 
5277  // If the queue is full, wait
5278  while (ctx->stop_flag == 0 &&
5279  ctx->sq_head - ctx->sq_tail >= (int) ARRAY_SIZE(ctx->queue)) {
5280  (void) pthread_cond_wait(&ctx->sq_empty, &ctx->mutex);
5281  }
5282 
5283  if (ctx->sq_head - ctx->sq_tail < (int) ARRAY_SIZE(ctx->queue)) {
5284  // Copy socket to the queue and increment head
5285  ctx->queue[ctx->sq_head % ARRAY_SIZE(ctx->queue)] = *sp;
5286  ctx->sq_head++;
5287  DEBUG_TRACE(("queued socket %d", sp->sock));
5288  }
5289 
5290  (void) pthread_cond_signal(&ctx->sq_full);
5291  (void) pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->mutex);
5292 }
5293 
5294 static int set_sock_timeout(SOCKET sock, int milliseconds) {
5295 #ifdef _WIN32
5296  DWORD t = milliseconds;
5297 #else
5298  struct timeval t;
5299  t.tv_sec = milliseconds / 1000;
5300  t.tv_usec = (milliseconds * 1000) % 1000000;
5301 #endif
5302  return setsockopt(sock, SOL_SOCKET, SO_RCVTIMEO, (void *) &t, sizeof(t)) ||
5303  setsockopt(sock, SOL_SOCKET, SO_SNDTIMEO, (void *) &t, sizeof(t));
5304 }
5305 
5306 static void accept_new_connection(const struct socket *listener,
5307  struct mg_context *ctx) {
5308  struct socket so;
5309  char src_addr[IP_ADDR_STR_LEN];
5310  socklen_t len = sizeof(so.rsa);
5311  int on = 1;
5312 
5313  if ((so.sock = accept(listener->sock, &so.rsa.sa, &len)) == INVALID_SOCKET) {
5314  } else if (!check_acl(ctx, ntohl(* (uint32_t *) &so.rsa.sin.sin_addr))) {
5315  sockaddr_to_string(src_addr, sizeof(src_addr), &so.rsa);
5316  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: %s is not allowed to connect", __func__, src_addr);
5317  closesocket(so.sock);
5318  } else {
5319  // Put so socket structure into the queue
5320  DEBUG_TRACE(("Accepted socket %d", (int) so.sock));
5321  set_close_on_exec(so.sock);
5322  so.is_ssl = listener->is_ssl;
5323  so.ssl_redir = listener->ssl_redir;
5324  getsockname(so.sock, &so.lsa.sa, &len);
5325  // Set TCP keep-alive. This is needed because if HTTP-level keep-alive
5326  // is enabled, and client resets the connection, server won't get
5327  // TCP FIN or RST and will keep the connection open forever. With TCP
5328  // keep-alive, next keep-alive handshake will figure out that the client
5329  // is down and will close the server end.
5330  // Thanks to Igor Klopov who suggested the patch.
5331  setsockopt(so.sock, SOL_SOCKET, SO_KEEPALIVE, (void *) &on, sizeof(on));
5332  set_sock_timeout(so.sock, atoi(ctx->config[REQUEST_TIMEOUT]));
5333  produce_socket(ctx, &so);
5334  }
5335 }
5336 
5337 static void *master_thread(void *thread_func_param) {
5338  struct mg_context *ctx = (struct mg_context *) thread_func_param;
5339  struct pollfd *pfd;
5340  int i;
5341 
5342  // Increase priority of the master thread
5343 #if defined(_WIN32)
5344  SetThreadPriority(GetCurrentThread(), THREAD_PRIORITY_ABOVE_NORMAL);
5345 #endif
5346 
5347 #if defined(ISSUE_317)
5348  struct sched_param sched_param;
5349  sched_param.sched_priority = sched_get_priority_max(SCHED_RR);
5350  pthread_setschedparam(pthread_self(), SCHED_RR, &sched_param);
5351 #endif
5352 
5353  pfd = (struct pollfd *) calloc(ctx->num_listening_sockets, sizeof(pfd[0]));
5354  while (pfd != NULL && ctx->stop_flag == 0) {
5355  for (i = 0; i < ctx->num_listening_sockets; i++) {
5356  pfd[i].fd = ctx->listening_sockets[i].sock;
5357  pfd[i].events = POLLIN;
5358  }
5359 
5360  if (poll(pfd, ctx->num_listening_sockets, 200) > 0) {
5361  for (i = 0; i < ctx->num_listening_sockets; i++) {
5362  // NOTE(lsm): on QNX, poll() returns POLLRDNORM after the
5363  // successfull poll, and POLLIN is defined as (POLLRDNORM | POLLRDBAND)
5364  // Therefore, we're checking pfd[i].revents & POLLIN, not
5365  // pfd[i].revents == POLLIN.
5366  if (ctx->stop_flag == 0 && (pfd[i].revents & POLLIN)) {
5367  accept_new_connection(&ctx->listening_sockets[i], ctx);
5368  }
5369  }
5370  }
5371  }
5372  free(pfd);
5373  DEBUG_TRACE(("stopping workers"));
5374 
5375  // Stop signal received: somebody called mg_stop. Quit.
5376  close_all_listening_sockets(ctx);
5377 
5378  // Wakeup workers that are waiting for connections to handle.
5379  pthread_cond_broadcast(&ctx->sq_full);
5380 
5381  // Wait until all threads finish
5382  (void) pthread_mutex_lock(&ctx->mutex);
5383  while (ctx->num_threads > 0) {
5384  (void) pthread_cond_wait(&ctx->cond, &ctx->mutex);
5385  }
5386  (void) pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->mutex);
5387 
5388  // All threads exited, no sync is needed. Destroy mutex and condvars
5389  (void) pthread_mutex_destroy(&ctx->mutex);
5390  (void) pthread_cond_destroy(&ctx->cond);
5391  (void) pthread_cond_destroy(&ctx->sq_empty);
5392  (void) pthread_cond_destroy(&ctx->sq_full);
5393 
5394 #if !defined(NO_SSL)
5395  uninitialize_ssl(ctx);
5396 #endif
5397  DEBUG_TRACE(("exiting"));
5398 
5399  // Signal mg_stop() that we're done.
5400  // WARNING: This must be the very last thing this
5401  // thread does, as ctx becomes invalid after this line.
5402  ctx->stop_flag = 2;
5403  return NULL;
5404 }
5405 
5406 static void free_context(struct mg_context *ctx) {
5407  int i;
5408 
5409  // Deallocate config parameters
5410  for (i = 0; i < NUM_OPTIONS; i++) {
5411  if (ctx->config[i] != NULL)
5412  free(ctx->config[i]);
5413  }
5414 
5415 #ifndef NO_SSL
5416  // Deallocate SSL context
5417  if (ctx->ssl_ctx != NULL) {
5418  SSL_CTX_free(ctx->ssl_ctx);
5419  }
5420  if (ssl_mutexes != NULL) {
5421  free(ssl_mutexes);
5422  ssl_mutexes = NULL;
5423  }
5424 #endif // !NO_SSL
5425 
5426  // Deallocate context itself
5427  free(ctx);
5428 }
5429 
5430 void mg_stop(struct mg_context *ctx) {
5431  ctx->stop_flag = 1;
5432 
5433  // Wait until mg_fini() stops
5434  while (ctx->stop_flag != 2) {
5435  (void) mg_sleep(10);
5436  }
5437  free_context(ctx);
5438 
5439 #if defined(_WIN32) && !defined(__SYMBIAN32__)
5440  (void) WSACleanup();
5441 #endif // _WIN32
5442 }
5443 
5444 struct mg_context *mg_start(const struct mg_callbacks *callbacks,
5445  void *user_data,
5446  const char **options) {
5447  struct mg_context *ctx;
5448  const char *name, *value, *default_value;
5449  int i;
5450 
5451 #if defined(_WIN32) && !defined(__SYMBIAN32__)
5452  WSADATA data;
5453  WSAStartup(MAKEWORD(2,2), &data);
5454  InitializeCriticalSection(&global_log_file_lock);
5455 #endif // _WIN32
5456 
5457  // Allocate context and initialize reasonable general case defaults.
5458  // TODO(lsm): do proper error handling here.
5459  if ((ctx = (struct mg_context *) calloc(1, sizeof(*ctx))) == NULL) {
5460  return NULL;
5461  }
5462  ctx->callbacks = *callbacks;
5463  ctx->user_data = user_data;
5464 
5465  while (options && (name = *options++) != NULL) {
5466  if ((i = get_option_index(name)) == -1) {
5467  cry(fc(ctx), "Invalid option: %s", name);
5468  free_context(ctx);
5469  return NULL;
5470  } else if ((value = *options++) == NULL) {
5471  cry(fc(ctx), "%s: option value cannot be NULL", name);
5472  free_context(ctx);
5473  return NULL;
5474  }
5475  if (ctx->config[i] != NULL) {
5476  cry(fc(ctx), "warning: %s: duplicate option", name);
5477  free(ctx->config[i]);
5478  }
5479  ctx->config[i] = mg_strdup(value);
5480  DEBUG_TRACE(("[%s] -> [%s]", name, value));
5481  }
5482 
5483  // Set default value if needed
5484  for (i = 0; config_options[i * 2] != NULL; i++) {
5485  default_value = config_options[i * 2 + 1];
5486  if (ctx->config[i] == NULL && default_value != NULL) {
5487  ctx->config[i] = mg_strdup(default_value);
5488  }
5489  }
5490 
5491  // NOTE(lsm): order is important here. SSL certificates must
5492  // be initialized before listening ports. UID must be set last.
5493  if (!set_gpass_option(ctx) ||
5494 #if !defined(NO_SSL)
5495  !set_ssl_option(ctx) ||
5496 #endif
5497  !set_ports_option(ctx) ||
5498 #if !defined(_WIN32)
5499  !set_uid_option(ctx) ||
5500 #endif
5501  !set_acl_option(ctx)) {
5502  free_context(ctx);
5503  return NULL;
5504  }
5505 
5506 #if !defined(_WIN32) && !defined(__SYMBIAN32__)
5507  // Ignore SIGPIPE signal, so if browser cancels the request, it
5508  // won't kill the whole process.
5509  (void) signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN);
5510  // Also ignoring SIGCHLD to let the OS to reap zombies properly.
5511  (void) signal(SIGCHLD, SIG_IGN);
5512 #endif // !_WIN32
5513 
5514  (void) pthread_mutex_init(&ctx->mutex, NULL);

5518 
5519  // Start master (listening) thread
5520  mg_start_thread(master_thread, ctx);
5521 
5522  // Start worker threads
5523  for (i = 0; i < atoi(ctx->config[NUM_THREADS]); i++) {
5524  if (mg_start_thread(worker_thread, ctx) != 0) {
5525  cry(fc(ctx), "Cannot start worker thread: %ld", (long) ERRNO);
5526  } else {
5527  ctx->num_threads++;
5528  }
5529  }
5530 
5531  return ctx;
5532 }
